info.title: OWASP Top 10 app security test script

diffs.patch:
Index: scripts/owasp_scan.py
===================================================================
--- scripts/owasp_scan.py	
+++ scripts/owasp_scan.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,864 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""OWASP Top 10 (2021) security scanner for the Bible Editorial AI app.
+
+Performs live black-box checks against a running deployment (backend API,
+frontend, n8n) and static checks against the repository source tree under the
+current directory.
+
+Quick start
+-----------
+    python scripts/owasp_scan.py                          # localhost defaults
+    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --api-base https://api.example.com
+    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --check-deps              # run pip/npm audits
+
+Exit code: 0 = no FAIL findings, 1 = at least one FAIL.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import base64
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+import urllib.parse
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+try:
+    import httpx
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
+    sys.exit("This scanner needs `httpx`. Install it:  python -m pip install httpx")
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+ANSI = {
+    "FAIL": "\033[91m",
+    "WARN": "\033[93m",
+    "INFO": "\033[96m",
+    "PASS": "\033[92m",
+    "BOLD": "\033[1m",
+    "END": "\033[0m",
+}
+
+
+class Check:
+    """One OWASP check result."""
+
+    def __init__(self, category, check_id, title, level, detail):
+        self.category = category
+        self.id = check_id
+        self.title = title
+        self.level = level
+        self.detail = detail
+
+    def to_dict(self):
+        return {
+            "category": self.category,
+            "id": self.id,
+            "title": self.title,
+            "level": self.level,
+            "detail": self.detail,
+        }
+
+    def __str__(self):
+        color = ANSI.get(self.level, "")
+        return (
+            f"  {color}{self.level.ljust(4)}{ANSI['END']} [{self.category}] "
+            f"{self.title}\n        \u2514 {self.detail}"
+        )
+
+
+def _b64url(raw):
+    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
+
+
+def make_jwt(secret: str, claims: dict, alg: str = "HS256") -> str:
+    head = _b64url(json.dumps({"alg": alg, "typ": "JWT"}).encode())
+    payload = _b64url(json.dumps(claims).encode())
+    signing = head + b"." + payload
+    if alg == "none":
+        return (signing + b".").decode()
+    sig = _b64url(hmac.new(secret.encode(), signing, hashlib.sha256).digest())
+    return (signing + b"." + sig).decode()
+
+
+class Scanner:
+    def __init__(self, api_base, frontend_base, n8n_base, check_deps, timeout):
+        self.api_base = api_base.rstrip("/")
+        self.frontend_base = frontend_base.rstrip("/")
+        self.n8n_base = n8n_base.rstrip("/")
+        self.check_deps = check_deps
+        self.timeout = timeout
+        self.results = []
+        self.client = httpx.Client(base_url=self.api_base, timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=False)
+        self.victim_token = ""
+        self.attacker_token = ""
+        self.victim_id = 0
+        self.attacker_id = 0
+        self.project_id = None
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
+
+    def add(self, category, check_id, title, level, detail):
+        self.results.append(Check(category, check_id, title, level, detail))
+
+    def email(self, tag):
+        return f"{tag}-{int(time.time())}-{abs(hash(tag)) % 10000}@example.net"
+
+    def req(self, method, path, token=None, json_body=None, headers=None, **kwargs):
+        h = dict(headers or {})
+        if token:
+            h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
+        return self.client.request(method, path, json=json_body, headers=h, **kwargs)
+
+    def jbody(self, resp):
+        if "json" not in resp.headers.get("content-type", ""):
+            return None
+        try:
+            return resp.json()
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def login(self, email, password):
+        """POST /auth/login with retry/backoff so the app's per-IP rate limit
+        (5 logins/min in the default config) does not abort the scan.
+        Returns the access token or None."""
+        waited = False
+        for _ in range(4):
+            r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/login",
+                         json_body={"email": email, "password": password})
+            if r.status_code == 200:
+                return self.jbody(r).get("access_token", "")
+            if r.status_code == 429:
+                if not waited:
+                    time.sleep(61)
+                    waited = True
+                else:
+                    time.sleep(15)
+                continue
+            return None
+        return None
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ recon
+
+    def _recon(self):
+        self._hdr_check("A05", "hdr-api", "API", self.api_base)
+        self._hdr_check("A05", "hdr-front", "Frontend", self.frontend_base)
+        for label, path in (("docs", "/docs"), ("openapi", "/openapi.json")):
+            try:
+                r = self.req("GET", path)
+                if r.status_code == 200:
+                    self.add("A00", f"recon-{label}", f"Surface: {label} exposed",
+                             "INFO", f"{path} -> HTTP 200 (API schema exposed)")
+                else:
+                    self.add("A00", f"recon-{label}", f"Surface: {label}",
+                             "PASS", f"{path} -> HTTP {r.status_code}, not exposed")
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.add("A00", f"recon-{label}", f"Surface: {label}", "FAIL", str(exc))
+        try:
+            r = self.req("GET", "/health")
+            self.add("A00", "recon-health", "API health endpoint",
+                     "PASS" if r.status_code == 200 else "FAIL",
+                     f"GET /health -> HTTP {r.status_code}")
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add("A00", "recon-health", "API health endpoint", "FAIL", f"Unreachable: {exc}")
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ A01
+
+    def _a01_broken_access_control(self):
+        cat = "A01"
+        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me")
+        self.add(cat, "unauth-protected", "Protected endpoints reject anonymous callers",
+                 "PASS" if r.status_code == 401 else "FAIL",
+                 f"GET /api/v1/auth/me w/o token -> HTTP {r.status_code} (expect 401)")
+
+        if not (self.victim_token and self.attacker_token and self.project_id):
+            self.add(cat, "idor", "Cross-user (IDOR) access denied",
+                     "WARN", "skipped (no victim/attacker context)")
+            return
+        for method, label, kwargs in (
+            ("GET", "read", {}),
+            ("PATCH", "modify", {"json_body": {"name": "hijacked"}}),
+            ("DELETE", "delete", {}),
+        ):
+            r = self.req(method, f"/api/v1/projects/{self.project_id}",
+                         token=self.attacker_token, **kwargs)
+            ok = r.status_code in (401, 403, 404)
+            self.add(cat, f"idor-{method.lower()}",
+                     f"IDOR: cross-user {label} of another user's project denied",
+                     "PASS" if ok else "FAIL",
+                     f"attacker {method} victim project #{self.project_id} -> "
+                     f"HTTP {r.status_code} (expect 401/403/404)")
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ A02
+
+    def _a02_cryptographic_failures(self):
+        cat = "A02"
+
+        # Live proof: JWT signing secret strength.
+        self._check_jwt_secret(cat)
+
+        # alg=none must be rejected.
+        tok = make_jwt("", {"sub": "1", "exp": int(time.time()) + 3600}, alg="none")
+        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me", token=tok)
+        self.add(cat, "jwt-none", "JWT 'alg=none' forgery rejected",
+                 "PASS" if r.status_code == 401 else "FAIL",
+                 f"unsigned token -> HTTP {r.status_code} (expect 401)")
+
+        # Wrong-secret token must be rejected.
+        tok = make_jwt("definitely-not-the-secret", {"sub": "1", "exp": int(time.time()) + 3600})
+        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me", token=tok)
+        self.add(cat, "jwt-wrong-secret", "JWT signed with wrong secret rejected",
+                 "PASS" if r.status_code == 401 else "FAIL",
+                 f"token signed with random secret -> HTTP {r.status_code} (expect 401)")
+
+        # Register response must not disclose credential material.
+        try:
+            r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/register", json_body={
+                "email": self.email("leak"), "password": "Str0ngPass!x",
+                "full_name": "leak", "is_admin": True, "hashed_password": "hunter2"})
+            leaked = "hunter2" in r.text or "hashed_password" in r.text or "password" in str(r.text).lower()
+            self.add(cat, "cred-leak", "API responses do not disclose password material",
+                     "FAIL" if leaked else "PASS",
+                     f"register w/ injected password fields -> HTTP {r.status_code}; "
+                     f"{'credential data leaked!' if leaked else 'no credential echo'}")
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add(cat, "cred-leak", "API responses do not disclose password material",
+                     "FAIL", str(exc))
+
+        # Transport security.
+        scheme = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.api_base).scheme
+        r = self.req("GET", "/health")
+        hsts = r.headers.get("strict-transport-security", "")
+        self.add(cat, "tls", "Transport security (HTTPS + HSTS)",
+                 "PASS" if (scheme == "https" and hsts) else "WARN",
+                 f"{self.api_base} scheme={scheme}, HSTS={'present' if hsts else 'absent'} "
+                 f"(prod must be HTTPS with HSTS)")
+
+    def _check_jwt_secret(self, cat):
+        """Live-verify whether the JWT HMAC secret can be guessed (token forgery).
+
+        If we already hold an issued token we can verify a candidate secret purely
+        offline via HMAC, then forge a token for a victim user id and confirm the
+        API accepts it. This is a real account-takeover proof.
+        """
+        tok = self.attacker_token or self.victim_token
+        if not tok:
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is strong",
+                     "WARN", "skipped (no issued token available)")
+            return
+        parts = tok.split(".")
+        if len(parts) != 3:
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is strong", "WARN",
+                     "unexpected token shape")
+            return
+        head, payload, sig_b64 = parts
+        sig = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(sig_b64 + "=" * (-len(sig_b64) % 4))
+        signing_input = f"{head}.{payload}".encode()
+
+        candidates = self._weak_secret_candidates()
+        matched = [c for c in candidates if hmac.new(c.encode(), signing_input, hashlib.sha256).digest() == sig]
+
+        if not matched:
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret not a known default",
+                     "PASS", f"HMAC did not match any of {len(candidates)} default/weak candidates")
+            return
+
+        secret = matched[0]
+        # Forge a token for the earliest (often highest-priv) user id and probe.
+        now = int(time.time())
+        forged = make_jwt(secret, {"sub": "1", "exp": now + 3600})
+        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me", token=forged)
+        body = self.jbody(r)
+        if r.status_code == 200:
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is weak/default -> token forgery",
+                     "FAIL", f"HMAC matched default secret candidate; forged token for user id 1 "
+                             f"accepted -> HTTP 200: {body!r}")
+        elif r.status_code == 401 and "iss" in body and body.get("detail") not in ("Invalid token",):
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is weak/default -> token forgery",
+                     "FAIL", "HMAC matched a default secret candidate (token signing compromised)")
+        else:
+            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is weak/default (forgery blocked by claims)",
+                     "FAIL",
+                     f"HMAC matched default candidate but forged token rejected HTTP {r.status_code}: {body!r}")
+
+    def _weak_secret_candidates(self):
+        cands = {
+            "change-me-in-production",
+            "change-me-in-production-change-me-in-production-1234",
+            "change-me", "secret", "password", "admin", "editorial", "localhost",
+            "bible-editorial-ai", "your-secret-key-here", "secret_key", "changeme",
+        }
+        env_file = REPO_ROOT / ".env"
+        if env_file.exists():
+            for line in env_file.read_text().splitlines():
+                if line.startswith("SECRET_KEY="):
+                    cands.add(line.split("=", 1)[1].strip())
+        cfg = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "app" / "core" / "config.py"
+        if cfg.exists():
+            for m in re.findall(r'SECRET_KEY[:\s]*=\s*"([^"]+)"', cfg.read_text()):
+                cands.add(m)
+        return cands
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ A03
+
+    def _a03_injection(self):
+        cat = "A03"
+        token = self.attacker_token
+        if not token:
+            self.add(cat, "sqli", "Injection resistance (SQL / XSS / header)",
+                     "WARN", "skipped (no attacker token)")
+            return
+
+        payloads = [
+            ("1' OR '1'='1", "single-quote boolean"),
+            ("1'; DROP TABLE projects; --", "stacked DROP"),
+            ("1 UNION SELECT 1,2,3,password FROM users--", "UNION from users"),
+        ]
+        for payload, about in payloads:
+            try:
+                name = f"sqltest {payload} {int(time.time())}"
+                r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/projects", token=token,
+                             json_body={"name": name, "description": about})
+                good = r.status_code in (200, 201)
+                self.add(cat, "sqli-create",
+                         "SQL injection via project name parametrized",
+                         "PASS" if good else "FAIL",
+                         f"payload={payload!r} -> HTTP {r.status_code}; "
+                         f"body={r.text[:80]!r}")
+                if r.status_code in (200, 201) and r.text:
+                    pid = self.jbody(r)
+                    if isinstance(pid, dict) and pid.get("id"):
+                        self.req("DELETE", f"/api/v1/projects/{pid['id']}", token=token)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.add(cat, "sqli-create", "Injection checks", "FAIL", str(exc))
+                break
+
+        # Stored-XSS payload: the API must treat it as opaque JSON data, never
+        # reflect it into an HTML context. (False-positive guard: echoing the
+        # stored value back inside a JSON response is expected and safe.)
+        xss_name = f"<script>alert(document.domain)</script> {int(time.time())}"
+        try:
+            rx = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/projects", token=token,
+                          json_body={"name": xss_name})
+            is_json = "json" in rx.headers.get("content-type", "")
+            html_reflected = "<script>alert" in rx.text and not is_json
+            self.add(cat, "xss-store",
+                     "Stored XSS payload handled as JSON data (not reflected to HTML)",
+                     "FAIL" if html_reflected else "PASS",
+                     f"stored {xss_name!r} -> HTTP {rx.status_code} "
+                     f"content-type={rx.headers.get('content-type', '?')} "
+                     f"html-reflected={html_reflected}")
+            if rx.status_code in (200, 201):
+                pid = self.jbody(rx)
+                if isinstance(pid, dict) and pid.get("id"):
+                    self.req("DELETE", f"/api/v1/projects/{pid['id']}", token=token)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add(cat, "xss-store", "Stored XSS payload handled as JSON data", "WARN", str(exc))
+
+        # Header injection via Content-Disposition filename (export).
+        try:
+            rp = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/projects", token=token,
+                          json_body={"name": "header-inject-test"})
+            if rp.status_code in (200, 201):
+                pid = self.jbody(rp)["id"]
+                ri = self.req("POST", f"/api/v1/projects/{pid}/items", token=token,
+                              json_body={"title": "abc\r\nX-Injected: 1",
+                                         "content_type": "study_note"})
+                item_id = self.jbody(ri).get("id") if ri.status_code in (200, 201) else None
+                leaked = "unverified"
+                if item_id:
+                    try:
+                        re_exp = self.req("GET",
+                                          f"/api/v1/projects/{pid}/items/{item_id}/export?format=md",
+                                          token=token)
+                        leaked = str(re_exp.headers.get("x-injected"))
+                    except Exception as exc:
+                        leaked = f"connection {type(exc).__name__}"
+                self.add(cat, "header-inject",
+                         "CRLF header injection blocked",
+                         "FAIL" if leaked == "True" else "PASS",
+                         f"CRLF title on export -> header leak={leaked} "
+                         f"(retrieved response: {getattr(locals().get('re_exp', None), 'status_code', 'n/a')})")
+                self.req("DELETE", f"/api/v1/projects/{pid}", token=token)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add(cat, "header-inject", "CRLF header injection blocked", "WARN", str(exc))
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ A04
+
+    def _a04_insecure_design(self):
+        cat = "A04"
+        # Password policy: too-short must be rejected.
+        r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/register", json_body={
+            "email": self.email("short"), "password": "1234567", "full_name": "short"})
+        self.add(cat, "pw-short", "Minimum password length enforced",
+                 "PASS" if r.status_code == 422 else "WARN",
+                 f"7-char password -> HTTP {r.status_code} (expect 422)")
+
+        # Weak-but-valid password accepted (no complexity policy).
+        r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/register", json_body={
+            "email": self.email("weak"), "password": "aaaaaaaa", "full_name": "weak"})
+        self.add(cat, "pw-complexity",
+                 "Password complexity / common-password checks",
+                 "WARN" if r.status_code in (200, 201) else "PASS",
+                 f"8-char 'aaaaaaaa' accepted -> HTTP {r.status_code}; "
+                 f"recommend NIST-style minimum + breach-list check")
+
+        # No MFA enforcement.
+        self.add(cat, "mfa", "Multi-factor authentication",
+                 "INFO", "no MFA/2FA support found (JWT bearer only)")
+
+        # Long-lived tokens.
+        self.add(cat, "token-life", "Token lifetime",
+                 "INFO", "ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES default 7 days; short-lived "
+                         "tokens reduce the blast radius of the weak-secret forgery")
+
+        # Account enumeration at registration.
+        reg = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/register", json_body={
+            "email": self.whoami_email, "password": "Str0ngPass!x", "full_name": "dup"})
+        self.add(cat, "enum-register",
+                 "User enumeration at registration",
+                 "WARN" if reg.status_code == 409 else "PASS",
+                 f"re-register existing email -> HTTP {reg.status_code} "
+                 f"(409 reveals an account exists)")
+
+        # No account lockout, only IP rate limiting (checked live in A07).
+        self.add(cat, "lockout", "Account lockout / failed-login throttling",
+                 "INFO", "no per-account lockout; relies on IP rate limiting")
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ A05
+
+    def _hdr_check(self, cat, cid, label, url):
+        required = {
+            "Content-Security-Policy": "Content-Security-Policy",
+            "Strict-Transport-Security": "Strict-Transport-Security",
+            "X-Content-Type-Options": "X-Content-Type-Options",
+            "X-Frame-Options": "X-Frame-Options",
+            "Referrer-Policy": "Referrer-Policy",
+            "Permissions-Policy": "Permissions-Policy",
+            "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy": "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy",
+            "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy": "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy",
+        }
+        try:
+            r = httpx.get(url, timeout=self.timeout)
+            present = [v for k, v in required.items() if r.headers.get(k)]
+            missing = [v for k, v in required.items() if not r.headers.get(k)]
+            if not missing:
+                level = "PASS"
+            elif set(missing) <= {"Content-Security-Policy"}:
+                level = "WARN"   # CSP missing is a warning, not a hard fail
+            else:
+                level = "FAIL"
+            self.add(cat, cid, f"Security headers on {label}",
+                     level,
+                     f"present=[{', '.join(present) or 'none'}] "
+                     f"missing=[{', '.join(missing) or 'none'}]")
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add(cat, cid, f"Security headers on {label}", "FAIL", str(exc))
+
+    def _a05_misconfiguration(self):
+        cat = "A05"
+        r = self.req("GET", "/health")
+        server = r.headers.get("server", "")
+        if server:
+            self.add(cat, "banner", "Server software banner",
+                     "WARN", f"Server header discloses: {server!r}")
+        else:
+            self.add(cat, "banner", "Server software banner", "PASS", "no Server header")
+
+        # CORS: evil origin must not be reflected.
+        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me",
+                     headers={"Origin": "https://evil.example.com"})
+        acao = r.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin", "")
+        corr = r.headers.get("cross-origin-resource-policy", "")
+        self.add(cat, "cors",
+                 "CORS origin policy (no reflection of untrusted origins)",
+                 "FAIL" if acao else "PASS",
+                 f"evil origin -> ACAO={acao!r} CORP={corr!r}")
+
+        # Error responses must not leak stack traces / SQL.
+        for body, about in (
+            ({"email": "not-an-email", "password": "x"}, "invalid email"),
+            ({"email": "a@b.com", "password": "short"}, "short password"),
+            (None, "non-JSON body"),
+        ):
+            r = self.req("POST", "/api/v1/auth/login", json_body=body)
+            evil = ("Traceback" in r.text) or ("line " in r.text and "File " in r.text) \
+                or ("psycopg" in r.text.lower()) or ("postgres" in r.text.lower())
+            self.add(cat, "err-leak", "Error responses stay clean (no stack/SQL leak)",
+                     "FAIL" if evil else "PASS",
+                     f"malformed login {about} -> HTTP {r.status_code} "
+                     f"leak={evil} body={r.text[:60]!r}")
+
+        # n8n workflow automation: default credentials pinned in docker-compose.
+        compose = REPO_ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"
+        defaults = "n/a"
+        if compose.exists():
+            s = compose.read_text()
+            m_user = re.search(r"N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER[^\n]*?\{[^:]*:-([\w.]+)", s)
+            m_pass = re.search(r"N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD[^\n]*?\{[^:]*:-([\w.]+)", s)
+            defaults = f"user={m_user.group(1) if m_user else '?'}, pass={m_pass.group(1) if m_pass else '?'}"
+        try:
+            r = httpx.get(f"{self.n8n_base}/rest/workflows", timeout=self.timeout)
+            unauth = r.status_code in (401, 403)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.add(cat, "n8n", "n8n has authentication enabled (no default credentials)",
+                     "INFO", f"could not probe ({exc}); compose defaults: {defaults}")
+            return
+        if not unauth:
+            self.add(cat, "n8n", "n8n has authentication enabled (no default credentials)",
+                     "WARN", f"unauthenticated /rest/workflows -> HTTP {r.status_code}; compose defaults {defaults}")
+        else:
+            self.add(cat, "n8n", "n8n has authentication enabled (no default credentials)",
+                     "INFO", f"unauthenticated /rest/workflows -> HTTP {r.status_code}; "
+                             f"compose defaults {defaults} (rotate before production)")
+
+    def _a06_vulnerable_components(self):
+        cat = "A06"
+        info = []

1: # Bible Editorial AI
2: 
3: > An AI-assisted editorial production platform for Bible and Christian book publishers.
4: 
5: Bible and Christian book publishing runs on thousands of hours of manual editorial work — drafting study notes and devotionals from scripture, routing content through editors and proofreaders, checking manuscripts against source translations, and preparing print-ready files. **Bible Editorial AI** is a single workspace that automates the drudge work while keeping the human in the loop: AI drafts, humans approve.
6: 
7: ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
8: ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.115+-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white)

14: ---
15: 
16: ## Features
17: 
18: ### AI-Powered Draft Generation
19: Generate study notes, devotionals, and reference entries from any Bible passage. The AI follows per-project style guides, uses the correct translation, and adapts tone to content type. Powered by **Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5** — falls back to offline demo mode when no API key is set.
20: 
21: ### Editorial Review Workflow
22: Content moves through a structured pipeline: **Draft → In Review → Approved → Published**. Each transition is logged with timestamps and author attribution. Full version history for every content item — compare any two versions side-by-side with word-level diff.
23: 
24: ### Inline & Verse-Level Comments
25: Threaded comments anchored to specific text selections or Bible verses. Click a comment to jump to the highlighted text in the editor. Comment roles: admin, editor, reviewer, proofreader can comment; viewers can read only.
26: 
27: ### Manuscript QA
28: AI-powered style guide checking scores manuscripts against project editorial rules (0–100), flags violations by severity (high/medium/low), and highlights issues inline. Regex-based offline rules work without an API key.
29: 
30: ### Translation Comparison
31: Compare any Bible passage across **ESV, NIV, KJV, NASB, NLT** in a side-by-side panel. Insert quotations directly into the editor. Powered by [api.bible](https://api.bible) (with key) or free [getBible](https://getbible.net) API (KJV/WEB).
32: 
33: ### Project-Level Roles & Permissions
34: Per-project membership with five roles: **admin, editor, reviewer, proofreader, viewer**. Permissions are enforced server-side — editors can edit content, reviewers can approve, viewers read only. Workspace-level fallback for seamless access.
35: 
36: ### Export
37: Structured Markdown and Word (.docx) export with metadata block (passage, status, date), footnotes, and cross-references. Clean formatting suitable for handoff to layout teams.
38: 
39: ### Dark & Light Theme
40: Persistent theme toggle with system preference detection. Professional design system with Inter/Lora fonts and lucide icons.

# Bible Editorial AI

> An AI-assisted editorial production platform for Bible and Christian book publishers.

Bible and Christian book publishing runs on thousands of hours of manual editorial work — drafting study notes and devotionals from scripture, routing content through editors and proofreaders, checking manuscripts against source translations, and preparing print-ready files. **Bible Editorial AI** is a single workspace that automates the drudge work while keeping the human in the loop: AI drafts, humans approve.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.115+-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white)
![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-18+-61DAFB?logo=react&logoColor=black)
![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-16+-4169E1?logo=postgresql&logoColor=white)
![Anthropic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic-Claude-D97757?logo=anthropic&logoColor=white)
![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-Compose-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=white)

---

## Features

### AI-Powered Draft Generation
Generate study notes, devotionals, and reference entries from any Bible passage. The AI follows per-project style guides, uses the correct translation, and adapts tone to content type. Powered by **Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5** — falls back to offline demo mode when no API key is set.

### Editorial Review Workflow
Content moves through a structured pipeline: **Draft → In Review → Approved → Published**. Each transition is logged with timestamps and author attribution. Full version history for every content item — compare any two versions side-by-side with word-level diff.

### Inline & Verse-Level Comments
Threaded comments anchored to specific text selections or Bible verses. Click a comment to jump to the highlighted text in the editor. Comment roles: admin, editor, reviewer, proofreader can comment; viewers can read only.

### Manuscript QA
AI-powered style guide checking scores manuscripts against project editorial rules (0–100), flags violations by severity (high/medium/low), and highlights issues inline. Regex-based offline rules work without an API key.

### Translation Comparison
Compare any Bible passage across **ESV, NIV, KJV, NASB, NLT** in a side-by-side panel. Insert quotations directly into the editor. Powered by [api.bible](https://api.bible) (with key) or free [getBible](https://getbible.net) API (KJV/WEB).

### Project-Level Roles & Permissions
Per-project membership with five roles: **admin, editor, reviewer, proofreader, viewer**. Permissions are enforced server-side — editors can edit content, reviewers can approve, viewers read only. Workspace-level fallback for seamless access.

### Export
Structured Markdown and Word (.docx) export with metadata block (passage, status, date), footnotes, and cross-references. Clean formatting suitable for handoff to layout teams.

### Dark & Light Theme
Persistent theme toggle with system preference detection. Professional design system with Inter/Lora fonts and lucide icons.

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Backend** | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL 16 |
| **AI** | Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 (with offline demo mode) |
| **Frontend** | React 18, Vite, React Router, framer-motion |
| **Migrations** | Alembic |
| **Testing** | pytest (87 tests), Vitest (34 tests) |
| **Containerization** | Docker / Docker Compose |

---

## Project Structure

```
bible-editorial-ai/
├── backend/                        # FastAPI service
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── api/v1/                 # REST endpoints
│   │   │   ├── auth.py             # Register / login / me
│   │   │   ├── projects.py         # Projects + member management
│   │   │   ├── content.py          # Content items, versions, comments
│   │   │   ├── drafts.py           # AI draft generation
│   │   │   ├── review.py           # Editorial transitions + approvals
│   │   │   ├── style.py            # AI style-guide checking
│   │   │   ├── exports.py          # Markdown / DOCX export
│   │   │   └── translations.py     # Bible translation comparison
│   │   ├── models/                 # SQLAlchemy models
│   │   ├── schemas/                # Pydantic request/response schemas
│   │   ├── services/               # LLM prompts, export, diff, translations
│   │   ├── core/                   # Config, security, JWT
│   │   └── db/                     # Session, base
│   ├── alembic/                    # Database migrations
│   ├── tests/                      # 57 pytest tests
│   └── pyproject.toml
├── frontend/                       # React UI
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── pages/                  # Login, Projects, ProjectDetail, Editor
│   │   ├── components/editor/      # ContentEditor, CommentsPanel, etc.
│   │   ├── hooks/                  # useEditor (state management)
│   │   ├── api/                    # API client
│   │   ├── permissions.js          # Role-based access helpers
│   │   └── __tests__/              # 32 Vitest tests
│   └── package.json
├── docker-compose.yml              # PostgreSQL + backend + frontend
├── .env.example                    # Environment template
└── scripts/seed.py                 # Demo data seeder
```

---

## Getting Started

### Option 1: Docker (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Sirius1616/bible-editorial-ai.git
cd bible-editorial-ai

# Configure
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env — add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for live AI (optional)

# Start everything
docker compose up --build
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| Frontend | http://localhost:3000 |
| Backend API | http://localhost:8000/docs |

**Demo login:** `demo@editorial.ai` / `demo-password-1`

### Option 2: Local development

```bash
# Database
docker compose up -d db

# Backend
cd backend
cp ../.env.example .env  # edit DATABASE_URL if needed
uv sync
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload   # → http://localhost:8000/docs

# Frontend (new terminal)
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev                              # → http://localhost:3000

# Seed demo data
cd .. && python scripts/seed.py
```

### Running tests

```bash
# Backend (57 tests)
cd backend && uv run pytest

# Frontend (32 tests)
cd frontend && npm test
```

---

## How It Works

### Editorial Workflow

```
Draft ──→ In Review ──→ Approved ──→ Published
  ↑           │
  └───────────┘  (rejected → back to draft)
```

Every transition is logged with author, timestamp, and optional note.

### AI Integration

The app uses **Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5** for these features:

| Feature | What it does | Response format |
|---|---|---|
| **AI Draft** | Writes editorial content from a Bible passage | Plain text |
| **Style Check** | Reviews a manuscript against the style guide | JSON (score + issues) |
| **Scripture QA** | Verifies quoted scripture against the anchored passage | JSON (score + issues) |
| **Consistency** | Validates cross-references and terminology drift | JSON (score + issues) |

Without an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, all features fall back to offline demo mode — the app works fully without paying for API calls.

### Role-Based Access

| Role | Can do |
|---|---|
| **Admin** | Everything + manage members + delete project |
| **Editor** | Edit content, generate drafts, export |
| **Reviewer** | Approve/reject content, comment |
| **Proofreader** | Comment, read content |
| **Viewer** | Read only |

---

## API Highlights

```
POST   /api/v1/auth/register          # Create account
POST   /api/v1/auth/login             # Get JWT token

GET    /api/v1/projects               # List projects
POST   /api/v1/projects               # Create project
GET    /api/v1/projects/:id/members   # List members
POST   /api/v1/projects/:id/members   # Add member

POST   /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/draft       # AI draft
POST   /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/style-check  # AI style check
POST   /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/versions     # Save version
POST   /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/transition    # Change status
GET    /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/export        # Download MD/DOCX
GET    /api/v1/projects/:pid/content/:iid/translations  # Compare translations
```

Full interactive docs at `http://localhost:8000/docs`.

---

## Roadmap

- [x] Editorial workflow (draft → review → approve → publish)
- [x] Version history + word-level diff

- [x] Translation comparison sidebar (ESV, NIV, KJV, NASB, NLT)
- [x] AI style-guide checking
- [x] Markdown + DOCX export
- [x] Dark/light theme
- [ ] Task assignment & workload views (#22)
- [ ] Notifications (#23)
- [ ] n8n workflow automations (#40)

import secrets

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware

from app.api.v1.router import api_router
from app.core.config import settings


class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    """Apply baseline hardening response headers to every reply (SPA + API)."""

    HEADERS = {
        "Strict-Transport-Security": "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains",
        "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
        "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
        "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
        "Permissions-Policy": "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()",
        "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy": "same-origin",
        "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy": "same-origin",
    }

    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next) -> Response:
        response: Response = await call_next(request)
        for header, value in self.HEADERS.items():
            response.headers.setdefault(header, value)
        return response


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    docs_enabled = settings.ENVIRONMENT != "production"
    app = FastAPI(
        title=settings.APP_NAME,
        version="0.1.0",
        description="AI-assisted editorial production platform for Bible publishers.",
        docs_url="/docs" if docs_enabled else None,
        redoc_url="/redoc" if docs_enabled else None,
        openapi_url="/openapi.json" if docs_enabled else None,
    )

    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)

    app.include_router(api_router, prefix="/api/v1")

    @app.get("/health", tags=["system"])
    def health() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok"}

    return app


app = create_app()

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import get_current_user
from app.core.ratelimit import rate_limit_client, rate_limit_register
from app.core.security import (
    DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH,
    create_access_token,
    hash_password,
    verify_password,
)
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.models.user import User
from app.models.workspace import Workspace, WorkspaceMember
from app.schemas.user import Token, UserCreate, UserLogin, UserOut

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])


@router.post(
    "/register",
    response_model=UserOut,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    dependencies=[Depends(rate_limit_register)],
)
def register(payload: UserCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> User:
    existing = db.scalar(select(User).where(User.email == payload.email))
    if existing is not None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Email already registered")
    user = User(
        email=payload.email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(payload.password),
        full_name=payload.full_name,
    )
    db.add(user)
    db.flush()
    workspace = Workspace(name=f"{payload.full_name}'s Workspace", owner_id=user.id)
    db.add(workspace)
    db.flush()
    db.add(
        WorkspaceMember(
            workspace_id=workspace.id, user_id=user.id, role="owner"
        )
    )
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)
    return user


@router.post("/login", response_model=Token, dependencies=[Depends(rate_limit_client)])
def login(payload: UserLogin, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Token:
    user = db.scalar(select(User).where(User.email == payload.email))
    hash_to_check = user.hashed_password if user is not None else DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH
    password_matches = verify_password(payload.password, hash_to_check)
    if user is None or not password_matches or not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid email or password",
        )
    return Token(access_token=create_access_token(user.id))


@router.post(
    "/me/deactivate",
    response_model=None,
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
)
def deactivate_me(
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> None:
    """Soft-delete the current account. Keeps all authored content / comments /
    history (no hard cascade) and immediate-rejects on the next request that
    carries a token. A re-login after this fails because is_active is False.
    """
    current_user.is_active = False
    current_user.deleted_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    db.commit()


@router.get("/me", response_model=UserOut)
def me(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
    return current_user

The user wants a script to test the app for OWASP Top 10. Best approach options:

1. **OWASP ZAP CLI (zaproxy)** - The gold standard. ZAP can do a full automated scan. The snap version is available. But running ZAP headless via snap can be finicky.

2. **A custom Python script using httpx** - This would be a self-contained script that targets the specific app's endpoints and checks for OWASP Top 10 issues:
   - A01: Broken Access Control
   - A02: Cryptographic Failures
   - A03: Injection
   - A04: Insecure Design
   - A05: Security Misconfiguration
   - A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
   - A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
   - A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
   - A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
   - A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

Given the app is running, a custom script that hits the live API endpoints is the most useful and testable. It can:
- Test auth: register, login with rate limiting (careful not to lock out), weak passwords, JWT token manipulation (check SECRET_KEY default, alg=none attack, expired tokens)
- Test broken access control: try accessing other users' projects, unauthorized role transitions
- Test injection: SQLi attempts in query params (FastAPI+SQLAlchemy parametrized queries should resist), NoSQL/XSS in content fields
- Test security misconfiguration: check security headers, CORS config, exposed /docs in production, JWT in localStorage, weak default secret
- Test crypto failures: passwords only over HTTPS, JWT secret strength, bcrypt used for passwords (good), check if sensitive fields are exposed in API responses
- Test SSRF: maybe check the translations endpoint which fetches Bible APIs
- Vulnerable components: check dependency versions
- Logging/monitoring: hard to test via API but can check for audit logs

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from fastapi.responses import Response
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import PROJECT_EXPORT_ROLES, ensure_project_role, get_current_user
from app.api.v1.projects import get_accessible_project
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.models.content import ContentItem, ContentVersion
from app.models.user import User
from app.services.export import export_docx, export_markdown

router = APIRouter(prefix="/projects/{project_id}/items/{item_id}/export", tags=["exports"])


@router.get("")
def export_item(
    project_id: int,
    item_id: int,
    format: str = "md",
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> Response:
    project = get_accessible_project(project_id, user, db)
    ensure_project_role(db, project, user, PROJECT_EXPORT_ROLES)
    item = db.get(ContentItem, item_id)
    if item is None or item.project_id != project.id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Content item not found")

    latest = db.scalar(
        select(ContentVersion)
        .where(ContentVersion.content_item_id == item.id)
        .order_by(ContentVersion.version_number.desc())
    )
    body = latest.body if latest else ""
    passage = item.verse_label() or item.passage or ""
    footnotes = latest.footnotes if latest else []
    cross_refs = latest.cross_refs if latest else []
    if format == "docx":
        filename = f"{item.title.replace(' ', '_').lower()}.docx"
        return Response(
            content=export_docx(item.title, body, passage, footnotes, cross_refs, item.status),
            media_type=(
                "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument."
                "wordprocessingml.document"
            ),
            headers={"Content-Disposition": f'attachment; filename="{filename}"'},
        )
    if format != "md":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Unsupported export format")
    filename = f"{item.title.replace(' ', '_').lower()}.md"
    return Response(
        content=export_markdown(item.title, body, passage, footnotes, cross_refs, item.status),
        media_type="text/markdown",
        headers={"Content-Disposition": f'attachment; filename="{filename}"'},
    )

router = APIRouter(prefix="/projects/{project_id}/items", tags=["translations"])


@router.get(
    "/{item_id}/translations",
    response_model=TranslationComparisonOut,
    dependencies=[Depends(rate_limit_style)],
)
async def get_translations(
    project_id: int,
    item_id: int,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> dict:
    project: Project = get_accessible_project(project_id, user, db)
    item = db.get(ContentItem, item_id)
    if item is None or item.project_id != project.id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Content item not found")

    if not (item.verse_start_book and item.verse_start_chapter and item.verse_start_verse):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Anchor this item to a passage before comparing translations.",
        )

    end_verse = None
    if (
        item.verse_end_book
        and item.verse_end_book == item.verse_start_book
        and item.verse_end_chapter == item.verse_start_chapter
    ):
        end_verse = item.verse_end_verse

    try:
        result, _demo = await fetch_passage(
            item.verse_start_book,
            item.verse_start_chapter,
            item.verse_start_verse,
            end_verse,
        )
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc))

    return result

The script should:
1. Cover all 10 OWASP Top 10 categories
2. Be safe (not destructive, avoid rate-limit lockout issues)
3. Produce a nice report

Let me think about what tests to include for each OWASP category against this FastAPI app:

**A01:2021 Broken Access Control (IDOR, privilege escalation)**
- Try to access another user's project by ID (create user B, try to read user A's project with B's token)
- Try to force role escalation (register then try to access admin-only endpoints)
- Check `GET /api/v1/auth/me` requires auth
- Check that deactivated user token is rejected
- Test CORS misconfig? No that's A05.

**A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures**
- Check if login/register endpoints transmit sensitive data (they do over HTTPS normally; local test is HTTP)
- JWT uses HS256 + strong secret - check secret strength (config default 'change-me...' — in .env it's 'change-me-in-production')
- Check bcrypt for password storage (good)
- Check if password or hashed password leaks in responses
- Test JWT alg confusion / 'none' algorithm
- JWT with wrong secret is rejected
- Check that tokens expire (ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES default 7 days - long but configurable)

**A03:2021 Injection**
- SQL injection attempts in query params, path params, JSON fields (obviously SQLAlchemy parametrizes, but pagination/order params might be vulnerable — check endpoints for raw query building)
- NoSQL/XSS reflected: submit `<script>alert(1)</script>` in project name, content body - check response (FastAPI would not reflect as HTML by default; might be safe)
- Check export format param — could be injection? It's validated against "md"/"docx"
- Content-Disposition filename injection — item.title includes quotes? Could header injection occur? FastAPI/Starlette validates headers.

**A04:2021 Insecure Design**
- No password policy on register (weak passwords allowed)
- No account lockout / unlimited login attempts (rate limiter exists: 5/min — that's decent)
- JWT long expiry (7 days)
- No CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints (Bearer token auth mitigates)
- No email verification

**A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration**
- Security headers present? (Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, CORP)
- Missing: Content-Security-Policy!
- `Server` header disclosure
- `/docs` / `/openapi.json` exposed in development (correctly disabled in production)
- CORS: allow_origins config, allow_credentials=True with specific origins (ok if origins specific)
- OpenAPI schema exposure
- dangerous: `database` errors leaking info
- n8n default creds admin/admin (hardcoded in docker-compose!)

**A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components**
- Check dependency versions (hard for a runtime script, but can check via pip/uv list)

**A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures**
- Rate limiting on login (5/min) - good
- Weak password policy on register (no min length? check schemas)

- JWT stored in localStorage? (frontend) 
- Password in query params? No.

**A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures**
- JWT with alg=none
- Unsigned/invalid JWT rejected
- Dependency integrity (pip, npm lockfiles — hard to test runtime)
- Check Content-Disposition filename injection maybe

**A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures**

def passage_reference(book: str, chapter: int, start_verse: int, end_verse: int | None = None) -> str:
    reference = f"{book} {chapter}:{start_verse}"
    if end_verse and end_verse != start_verse:
        reference += f"-{end_verse}"
    return reference


def dataset_key(book: str, chapter: int, start_verse: int, end_verse: int | None = None) -> str:
    key = f"{book.strip().lower()} {chapter}:{start_verse}"
    if end_verse and end_verse != start_verse:
        key += f"-{end_verse}"
    return key


def demo_comparison(reference: str, kjv: str, web: str) -> dict:
    entries = [
        {"name": "KJV", "text": kjv, "available": True, "demo": True},
        {"name": "WEB", "text": web, "available": True, "demo": True},
    ]
    for name in settings.bible_translations:
        if name in {"KJV", "WEB"}:
            continue
        entries.append({"name": name, "text": None, "available": False, "demo": True})
    return {
        "reference": reference,
        "translations": entries,
        "demo": True,
        "note": (
            "Demo data — KJV and WEB are public domain. "
            "Set BIBLE_API_KEY (api.bible) to load ESV, NIV, NASB, and NLT."
        ),
    }


def _text_from_getbible(data: dict) -> str:
    verses: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    for block in data.values():
        for verse in block.get("verses", []):
            verses.append((int(verse["verse"]), verse["text"].strip()))
    verses.sort()
    return " ".join(text for _, text in verses)


async def _fetch_apibible(client: httpx.AsyncClient, translation: str, reference: str) -> str:
    bible_id = TRANSLATION_IDS[translation]
    response = await client.get(
        f"{BIBLE_API_URL}/bibles/{bible_id}/passages/{reference}",
        params={"content-type": "text"},
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()
    return data.get("data", {}).get("content", "").strip()


async def _fetch_getbible(client: httpx.AsyncClient, module: str, reference: str) -> str:
    response = await client.get(f"{GETBIBLE_URL}/{module}/{reference}")
    response.raise_for_status()
    return _text_from_getbible(response.json())


async def fetch_passage(
    book: str, chapter: int, start_verse: int, end_verse: int | None = None
) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
    reference = passage_reference(book, chapter, start_verse, end_verse)

    if settings.BIBLE_API_KEY:
        entries = []
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(
            timeout=60, headers={"api-key": settings.BIBLE_API_KEY}
        ) as client:
            for name in settings.bible_translations:
                if name not in TRANSLATION_IDS:
                    continue
                try:
                    text = await _fetch_apibible(client, name, reference)
                except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
                    if exc.response.status_code == 404:
                        entries.append(
                            {"name": name, "text": None, "available": False, "demo": False}
                        )
                        continue
                    if exc.response.status_code == 401:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "api.bible rejected the API key (401). Check BIBLE_API_KEY."
                        ) from exc
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"api.bible returned an error ({exc.response.status_code}). Try again later."
                    ) from exc
                except httpx.RequestError as exc:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        "Could not reach api.bible. Check your network connection."
                    ) from exc
                entries.append({"name": name, "text": text, "available": True, "demo": False})
        return {"reference": reference, "translations": entries, "demo": False, "note": None}, False

    bundled = DEMO_DATASET.get(dataset_key(book, chapter, start_verse, end_verse))
    if bundled:
        return demo_comparison(reference, bundled[0], bundled[1]), True

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60) as client:
        try:
            kjv = await _fetch_getbible(client, "kjv", reference)
            web = await _fetch_getbible(client, "web", reference)
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"getBible returned an error ({exc.response.status_code}). Try again later."
            ) from exc
        except httpx.RequestError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not reach getBible for the demo passage lookup. Check your network connection."
            ) from exc
    return demo_comparison(reference, kjv, web), True

    def _check_jwt_secret(self, cat):
        """Live-verify whether the JWT HMAC secret can be guessed (token forgery).

        If we already hold an issued token we can verify a candidate secret purely
        offline via HMAC, then forge a token for a victim user id and confirm the
        API accepts it. This is a real account-takeover proof.

        if not tok:
            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is strong",
                     "WARN", "skipped (no issued token available)")

        parts = tok.split(".")
        if len(parts) != 3:
            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is strong", "WARN",
                     "unexpected token shape")
            return
        head, payload, sig_b64 = parts
        sig = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(sig_b64 + "=" * (-len(sig_b64) % 4))
        signing_input = f"{head}.{payload}".encode()

        candidates = self._weak_secret_candidates()
        matched = [c for c in candidates if hmac.new(c.encode(), signing_input, hashlib.sha256).digest() == sig]

            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret not a known default",
                     "PASS", f"HMAC did not match any of {len(candidates)} default/weak candidates")

        now = int(time.time())
        forged = make_jwt(secret, {"sub": "1", "exp": now + 3600})
        r = self.req("GET", "/api/v1/auth/me", token=forged)
        body = self.jbody(r)

                     "FAIL", f"HMAC matched default secret candidate; forged token for user id 1 "
                             f"accepted -> HTTP 200: {body!r}")
        elif r.status_code == 401 and "iss" in body and body.get("detail") not in ("Invalid token",):
            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is weak/default -> token forgery",
                     "FAIL", "HMAC matched a default secret candidate (token signing compromised)")
        else:
            self.add(cat, "jwt-secret", "JWT signing secret is weak/default (forgery blocked by claims)",
                     "FAIL",
                     f"HMAC matched default candidate but forged token rejected HTTP {r.status_code}: {body!r}")

    def _weak_secret_candidates(self):
        cands = {
            "change-me-in-production",
            "change-me-in-production-change-me-in-production-1234",
            "change-me", "secret", "password", "admin", "editorial", "localhost",
            "bible-editorial-ai", "your-secret-key-here", "secret_key", "changeme",
        }
        env_file = REPO_ROOT / ".env"
        if env_file.exists():
            for line in env_file.read_text().splitlines():
                if line.startswith("SECRET_KEY="):
                    cands.add(line.split("=", 1)[1].strip())
        cfg = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "app" / "core" / "config.py"
        if cfg.exists():
            for m in re.findall(r'SECRET_KEY[:\s]*=\s*"([^"]+)"', cfg.read_text()):
                cands.add(m)
        return cands

parts.text:
The scanner works well. But there are bugs to fix:

1. **XSS reflect is a false positive**: The API returns JSON. The response text contains the payload because the STORED value is echoed back in JSON (`"name": "<script>..."`). def _hdr_check(self, cat, cid, label, url):
        required = {
            "Content-Security-Policy": "Content-Security-Policy",
            "Strict-Transport-Security": "Strict-Transport-Security",
            "X-Content-Type-Options": "X-Content-Type-Options",
            "X-Frame-Options": "X-Frame-Options",
            "Referrer-Policy": "Referrer-Policy",
            "Permissions-Policy": "Permissions-Policy",
            "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy": "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy",
            "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy": "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy",
        }
        try:
            r = httpx.get(url, timeout=self.timeout)
            present = [v for k, v in required.items() if r.headers.get(k)]
            missing = [v for k, v in required.items() if not r.headers.get(k)]
            if not missing:
                level = "PASS"
            elif set(missing) <= {"Content-Security-Policy"}:
                level = "WARN"   # CSP missing is a warning, not a hard fail
            else:
                level = "FAIL"
            self.add(cat, cid, f"Security headers on {label}",
                     level,
                     f"present=[{', '.join(present) or 'none'}] "
                     f"missing=[{', '.join(missing) or 'none'}]")
        except Exception as exc:
            self.add(cat, cid, f"Security headers on {label}", "FAIL", str(exc))

1. The scanner should tolerate 429 on *setup* logins — if rate-limited, sleep and retry with backoff (up to ~65s). Because repeatedly running the scanner will trip the shared IP limiter.
2. The brute-force test inherently hits the limiter (by design). After it 429s, subsequent logins are blocked for up to 60s. That's fine as it's last.

Let me implement a `_login` helper with retry/backoff and also add a small sleep to stagger. And make setup retry.

Implementation: 
```
def _login(self, email, password, retries=8, delay=8.0):
    for i in range(retries):
        r = self.req("POST","/api/v1/auth/login", json_body={...})
        if r.status_code == 200: return token
        if r.status_code == 429:

    return None

But better to just wait for the whole 60s window once: when first 429 seen, sleep 61s once, then up to 3 more retries. On a 5/min limiter, sleeping 61s guarantees a fresh bucket. So:

        if 429 and not waited: time.sleep(61); waited=True; continue
        if 429: sleep 15; continue

There's a redundant/contradictory pair of enum-login results: one INFO (skipped due to 429) and one FAIL from my retry handler that got 429s with t=0. I need to fix the enum-login logic: it shouldn't emit two conflicting checks, and a 429 shouldn't become a FAIL. Let me rewrite that section cleanly — the second attempt also got 429 (limiter persisted), and I marked it FAIL which is wrong (the app correctly rate-limited; it didn't reveal enumeration).

Let me rewrite enum-login to:
- attempt wrong-pw login
- attempt unknown login
- if either 429 → report PASS "rate limited, could not compare" or INFO. Since rate limiting itself prevents enumeration, that's acceptable: mark as PASS with note "rate-limiting active".
- else compare bodies.

Simpler rewrite:

```
r_wrong = req(wrong)
if r_wrong.status_code == 429:
    add enum-login PASS "limiter returned 429; account-existence oracle is rate-limited"
    return
r_unknown = req(unknown)
if r_unknown.status_code == 429:
    add INFO "partial: rate-limited mid-test" (rare)
    return
compare bodies/timing → PASS/FAIL
```

This will run: with the current live limiter, the first probe triggers 429 (since bucket full after brute force... wait order: enumeration runs BEFORE brute force. The bucket was full already from the previous runs within the same window? In this run, the enum-login got two 429s then brute-force got 429 immediately → bucket was already near-full at the start of A07. That's because my previous scanner run's logins (~15 min ago) plus... no, 60s bucket only. This run's logins: victim, attacker (setup) = 2. Then enum = 2 more = 4. Hmm 429 appeared at enum, meaning bucket already at 5. The wrong-pw + unknown from the *previous* full-run (15:50) would have reset by 60s. Unless the bucket window includes both runs (aligned 60s windows from monotonic start).

Whatever — after fixing, on a fresh run it'll behave properly. The important thing is: enum-login now handles 429 as PASS note, not FAIL.

Let me rewrite that whole enum-login segment.
Rate limiting works (429 hit). But the `enum-login` check double-emitted a bogus FAIL when the limiter replied 429. Let me rewrite it to treat rate-limiting as the correct outcome:

The scanner already supports `--api-base`, `--frontend-base`, `--no-bruteforce`, `--report`. So:

Command:
```bash

  --api-base https://<backend>.up.railway.app \
  --frontend-base https://<frontend>.up.railway.app \
  --report owasp_prod.json
```

Recommendations for launched instance:
1. Use `--no-bruteforce` on a shared production instance — the login limiter is per-IP, and 12 rapid attempts + enum probes could lock out real users behind the same public IP/NAT for 60s. The enum-login does 2 logins per run.
   - Actually with `--no-bruteforce`, the enum-login still does 2 login attempts. That's minimal. Fine.
2. Weak-secret check: works remotely — it verifies the HMAC signature of a real issued token against repo/.env candidates. If the launched app uses a different (strong) secret, it reports PASS. The candidate list is local; if the deployed secret is weak but not in the list, it won't be found. So this check is really about the known-default/leaked-secret case.
3. Registration: the scanner creates its own test users. If the launched backend disabled registration (or has captcha/email verification), `_setup_accounts` will fail and only recon/header checks run. That's a graceful limitation.
4. If they don't want the scanner to create accounts on production, they could reuse their own credentials — but the scanner doesn't support passing creds. Could mention they can add it, but keep it simple.
5. HTTPS: the A02 TLS check will now be relevant (scheme=https).

Let me keep the answer concise per the guidelines. Provide the command and caveats.

The scanner already supports that — point the `--api-base`/`--frontend-base` flags at the launched URLs. Since you deploy via Railway (`.railway/railway.ts`), for example:

```bash
python scripts/owasp_scan.py \
  --api-base https://your-backend.up.railway.app \
  --frontend-base https://your-frontend.up.railway.app \
  --report owasp_prod.json
```

Things to know when targeting the launched app:

- **Use `--no-bruteforce` on a shared production instance.** The login rate limiter is per-IP (5/min), so 12 rapid login attempts + the enumeration probes can temporarily 429 real users who share the same public IP/NAT. Add: `python scripts/owasp_scan.py --api-base https://... --no-bruteforce`
- **The weak-secret JWT test still works remotely.** It verifies the HMAC signature of a real token the app issues (you have to be able to register/login) against the weak-secret candidates, then forges a token — so it catches the `change-me-in-production` leak on your launched app too. If a deployed instance uses a strong random secret, it reports PASS.
- **Registration must be open.** The scan registers two throwaway `@example.net` accounts. If your production build disables sign-ups or requires email/MFA/captcha, `_setup_accounts` fails gracefully and only the recon + header checks run.
- **The TLS/HSTS check (A02) finally matters** — against `https://...` it validates HSTS instead of warning about plain HTTP.
- The n8n check and static repo checks (`.env`, lockfiles, deserialization sinks) still run from your local source tree, which is fine — they describe what you ship.

Want me to add a `--credentials` option so you can test the launched app against your own existing account instead of creating test users?

The user wants to make the scanner general-purpose so it can be used against any launched application, not just this specific Bible Editorial AI app. They want it to "print out places where there are vulnerabilities." So this is a request to generalize `scripts/owasp_scan.py` into a generic web/API OWASP scanner that: 1. Works against any launched application (not hardcoded to this app's endpoints) 2. Prints/enumerates the exact places (endpoints/URLs) where vulnerabilities exist The current scanner is heavily specialized: it registers accounts at `/api/v1/auth/register`, logs in at `/api/v1/auth/login`, creates projects at `/api/v1/projects`, checks `whoami_email`, does IDOR tests specific to this API, checks the secret candidates from this repo's `.env`/config.py, etc. A generic scanner needs to: - Take a target URL (and maybe a login form / API auth) - Crawl/discover endpoints (from OpenAPI if available, or crawl HTML links, or from a provided list) - Run OWASP Top 10 checks against discovered endpoints generically: - A01: Broken access control → test unauthenticated access on all discovered endpoints, check that sensitive endpoints require auth, IDOR heuristic (path params), etc. - A02: Crypto failures → HTTPS/HSTS checks, cookie secure/httpOnly flags - A03: Injection → send SQLi/XSS payloads to all endpoints (a mini-fuzzer), parametric checks, timing - A04: Insecure design → headers, etc. - A05: Misconfig → security headers, CORS wildcard, server banner, directory listing, common files (.env, .git, backup files, admin panels, exposed docs) - A06: Vulnerable components → version fingerprinting + optional audits - A07: Auth failures → cookie flags, login response equivalence, rate limiting (optional), common default paths, password policy - A08: Integrity → alg=none JWT? maybe generic; dependency lockfiles - A09: Logging → static, generic guidance - A10: SSRF → look for URL params/fields and test with echo services And crucially: "prints out places where there are vulnerabilities" — for each vulnerability found, output the exact URL (method + path + params) where it was found. So the finding should include the location. Approach: - Write a new generic scanner (or generalize the existing one). Given the existing script is deeply intertwined with this app, the cleanest is to create a NEW generic scanner `scripts/generic_owasp_scan.py` (or maybe generalize by refactoring). But the user said "make it in such a way that I can use it for general testing rather than just this testing." They may want the same script generalized. But keeping the app-specific one is valuable. I think best: create a generic scanner that can: 1. Discover endpoints via OpenAPI (if exposed) or a provided endpoint list (from a file/CLI) or crawl. 2. Run generic OWASP checks per endpoint. 3. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""OWASP Top 10 (2021) web application scanner — generic, any target.

Black-box scanner for ANY launched web app, plus an optional generic
source-code linter. It auto-discovers endpoints (OpenAPI / Swagger, robots.txt,
sitemap.xml, common paths), probes them for OWASP Top 10 weaknesses, and prints
the exact URLs (>places with vulnerabilities<). Optionally scans a source tree
and reports findings as file:line locations.

Usage
-----
    # Generic live scan of any app
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com

    # Scan several targets, Write a JSON report, add an auth header
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://a.example.com https://b.example.com \
        --report out.json -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"

    # Login to a target (auto-register or provided credentials) for deeper checks
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --creds user:pass
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --auth auto-register

    # Static source scan of a repository tree
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --code /path/to/src --report code.json

    # Run dependency audits (pip/npm) as well
    python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --check-deps

Exit code: 0 = no findings, 1 = at least one FAIL/CRITICAL/HIGH finding, 2 = error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import html
import json
import os
import random
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    import httpx
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit("This scanner needs `httpx`. Install it: python -m pip install httpx")

ANSI = {
    "FAIL": "\033[91m", "CRITICAL": "\033[95m", "HIGH": "\033[91m",
    "WARN": "\033[93m", "MEDIUM": "\033[93m", "INFO": "\033[96m", "LOW": "\033[96m",
    "PASS": "\033[92m", "BOLD": "\033[1m", "END": "\033[0m",
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vulnerability model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class Vuln:
    """A single weakness, always carrying the exact location where it lives."""

    issue: str
    location: str              # "GET https://host/path?param=..." or "src/x.py:12"
    category: str              # A01..A10 or "A00"/"code"
    severity: str              # CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | INFO | PASS
    evidence: str = ""
    remediation: str = ""

    SEV_ORDER = {"CRITICAL": 0, "HIGH": 1, "MEDIUM": 2, "LOW": 3, "INFO": 4, "PASS": 5}

    def __str__(self):
        color = ANSI.get(self.severity, "")
        pad = self.severity.ljust(8)
        text = f"  {color}{pad}{ANSI['END']} [{self.category}] {self.issue}\n        \u2514 {self.location}"
        if self.evidence:
            text += f"\n        \u2514 ev: {self.evidence[:220]}"
        if self.remediation:
            text += f"\n        \u2514 fix: {self.remediation}"
        return text

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "issue": self.issue,
            "location": self.location,
            "category": self.category,
            "severity": self.severity,
            "evidence": self.evidence,
            "remediation": self.remediation,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def sort_key(v):
        return (v.SEV_ORDER.get(v.severity, 9), v.category, v.location)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _b64url(raw: bytes) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")


def make_jwt(secret: str, claims: dict, alg: str = "HS256") -> str:
    head = _b64url(json.dumps({"alg": alg, "typ": "JWT"}).encode())
    payload = _b64url(json.dumps(claims).encode())
    signing = head + b"." + payload
    if alg == "none":
        return (signing + b".").decode()
    sig = _b64url(hmac.new(secret.encode(), signing, hashlib.sha256).digest())
    return (signing + b"." + sig).decode()


def first_existing(*paths: str) -> str | None:
    for p in paths:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            return p
    return None


def parse_creds(spec: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    if ":" not in spec:
        return None
    user, _, pwd = spec.partition(":")
    return user, pwd


EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")


def looks_like_email(value: str) -> bool:
    return bool(EMAIL_RE.match(value))

+# ===========================================================================
+# Static source-code scanner (generic, language-agnostic heuristics)
+# ===========================================================================
+
+SOURCE_PATTERNS = [
+    # (label, regex, severity, category)
+    ("Hardcoded secret-like assignment", r"(?i)\b(password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|"
+     r"pem|private[_-]?key)\b\s*[:=]\s*['\"][^'\"]{6,}", "HIGH", "A08"),
+    ("eval()/exec() of dynamic code", r"\b(eval|exec|execute)\s*\(\s*[^'\"]", "HIGH", "A03"),
+    ("Shell command via shell=True", r"subprocess\s*\.\s*(run|call|Popen|check_output)\s*\([^)]*shell\s*=\s*True",
+     "HIGH", "A03"),
+    ("os.system() shell call", r"\bos\.system\s*\([^)]*\)", "MEDIUM", "A03"),
+    ("SQL built by string concatenation", r"(execute|executemany|exec|query|cursor)\.?\s*\(\s*f?['\"].*?['\"].*?(%|\+|format\()",
+     "MEDIUM", "A03"),
+    ("Unsafe deserialization (pickle/yaml.load)", r"(pickle\.loads?\s*\(|yaml\.load\s*\([^)]*[,)])",
+     "HIGH", "A08"),
+    ("JWT decoded without verification", r"jwt\.(decode|verify)\s*\([^)]*verify\s*=\s*False|"
+     r"jwt\.decode\s*\([^)]*(algorithms\s*=\s*\[\s*['\"]none)",
+     "CRITICAL", "A08"),
+    ("TLS verification disabled", r"(verify\s*=\s*False|curl\.exe\(\).*--insecure|-k\b)",
+     "HIGH", "A02"),
+    ("Insecure cookie assignment", r"document\.cookie\s*=|\.cookie\s*=\s*['\"][^'\"]*",
+     "LOW", "A07"),
+    ("innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML", r"\.innerHTML\s*=|dangerouslySetInnerHTML",
+     "MEDIUM", "A03"),
+    ("CORS wildcard allowed", r"allow_origins\s*=\s*\[\s*['\"]\*\s*['\"]\s*\]|AddCors\s*\([^)]*AllowAnyOrigin",
+     "HIGH", "A05"),
+    ("Wide-open debug flag", r"debug\s*=\s*True|app\.debug\s*=\s*True|DEBUG\s*=\s*True",
+     "LOW", "A05"),
+]
